Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this mouthwatering Premier League game between Manchester United and Tottenham at Old Trafford.

If Manchester City had not entered a legal battle with the Premier League after being found guilty of breaching 114 charges relating to financial regulations by an independent panel, then surely there would be more pressure on the two head coaches in the dugout this evening?

Sources indicate that man Utd and Tottenham have undoubtedly both endured extremely disappointing starts to their respective top-flight campaigns. The hosts sit just inside the bottom half of the table after picking up just five points from their opening five matches. It’s going even worse for Tottenham, who languish in 20th with zero wins and just two points.

The perilous landscape leaves only one reasonable conclusion: this has all the ingredients for an early season six-pointer.

The strain is perhaps less intense on Michael Carrick, with the Englishman having built up a bundle of goodwill after cleaning up the mess left by Ruben Amorim last season as Man Utd eventually finished third, qualifying for the Champions League. Fans were left slightly underwhelmed by the club’s transfer window, with the players at Carrick’s disposal having not forged any momentum so far in this campaign.

The spotlight is definitely shining more intensely upon Roberto De Zerbi after substantial-spending Tottenham splashed over £300m in the summer on the likes of Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes, Jan Paul van Hecke and Savio. However, the Italian boss is yet to strike the correct rhythm with his newly-formed squad. An encouraging performance backed up by a positive result here at Old Trafford could be the perfect antidote to ease the worries of fans fearing that Tottenham could be embroiled in another relegation battle.

All eyes are on this one. Kick-off is at 17:30, with team news coming shortly.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that one of the major disappointments from this summer of change was seeing Hammers’ academy graduate Freddie Potts leave the club where he’d been since he was a seven year old. A ten million transfer fee justified the move in most fans’ minds, but there was still a sense of unfulfilled promise, despite Potts’ finally achieving his dream of a Premier League debut for the team he loved and had supported as a child.

In a candid interview today with BBC.co.uk, Potts reveals why he chose to quit West Ham United.

Without putting too fine a point on it, the whole move to Belgian Champions FC Brugge came about through manager Nuno Espirito Santo’s selection choices and Potts being sidelined, as he explained:.

“In pre-season my minutes with West Ham were limited, they weren’t as much as I wanted and then I spoke with my agent and remarked ‘let’s explore options because this season I’m 22, turning 23’,” Potts said.

“It’s a massive part of my career and I wanted to play.”.

Nuno’s decision to limit Potts’ game time led to his decision to quit the club.

Subsequently the interest from Brugge- now competing in the Champions League against the likes of Liverpool this very week – arose and Potts grabbed at the chance:.

“The opportunity of Club Brugge came along with Champions League football, the best club in Belgium and it was an opportunity I couldn’t really turn down with how my minutes were going down with West Ham.

According to recent reports, “I grew up in the area, going to the stadium watching the games. It was always going to be a tough decision but it was something that I had to do for my career.”.

Industry observers note that and who can blame him: Freddie lines up against Liverpool this week in the Champions League – the same week in which his old club head for a second division mid table scrap with Portsmouth. Good decision young man. Go and win it.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By TAMARA PRENN, SENIOR SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 10:38 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 11:29 EST, 23 November 2026.

Bayern Munich have come under criticism from FIFA's players' union and leading figures in the game amid accusations that the club is attempting to slash Jamal Musiala's wages following his diagnosis with a 'neurological dysfunction'.

The Germany international was diagnosed over the summer with absence seizures, a form of epilepsy which causes 'brief but easily treatable seizures'.

Musiala shocked the sporting world when he collapsed in two matches earlier this season, with Bayern manager Vincent Kompany explaining that the player had suffered from a reaction to a change in his medication.

Comments from members of Bayern's hierarchy have sparked controversy in Germany and abroad, with senior figures appearing to question the length of the player's contract – which runs until 2030 – should Musiala not recover his form.

Honorary president Uli Hoeness was the first to speak out on the potential drop-off in form Musiala might suffer with long-term absences, claiming earlier this month that he 'may never regain the performance level he once had'.

'We are facing a dilemma in this case, as he is suffering from an illness that cannot simply be cured, but it can be controlled to a certain extent with the use of medication,' Hoeness told German outlet BR24.

Fifpro and international footballers have come out in support of Musiala over concerns that Bayern Munich might reduce his salary.

Both Uli Hoeness and Karl-Heinz Rummenigge have made comments suggesting consequences should Musiala not return to his level.

Jan-Christian Dreesen also suggested that the club would need to 'assess' the situation if his performances do not return to their high heights.

Chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen then backed up Hoeness's comments and implied that Musiala's contract may need to be 'assessed'.

'We're monitoring his level of play. He'll certainly need time to improve further – like any injured player,' Dreesen noted in discussion with AZ. 'And then we need to calmly assess the situation and, if necessary, sit down with his family and management.

'Either we'll all be happy together and he'll be the same Jamal he always was – or, if he's a different Jamal along the way, we'll have to discuss it.'.

Recent findings suggest that 'If we're not consistently at a level that also aligns with the economic realities, then we'll have to talk to each other. Nevertheless, we have a valid contract, and that's the end of it.'.

According to recent reports, the 23-year-old is one of Bayern's highest-earners, having signed a deal with the club to extend his time in Bavaria in February 2025. The deal is thought to be worth £18.4million per year.

Adding fuel to the fire days later was former CEO Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, who told Sky Sports/RTL that he thought it was almost reasonable to discuss a renegotiation should Musiala not return to the level at which he once played.

It has been revealed that 'That is certainly possible and cannot be ruled out,' he said. 'Unfortunately, what we know suggests that it will be difficult to reach the level that he has so often shown here in this stadium.'.

In a recent development, 'We need to talk to the family, the player, and above all, the agency. Because then these sums are – sorry, with all due respect – no longer feasible.

'I can't imagine Jamal leaving the club or another club buying him under these circumstances. That's a problem. I think we handled this very sensitively with the player, and we're all interested in him coming back - ideally in top form. But what happens if that's not the case? Then we'll still have to think about the finances. And that's a task that the board and the supervisory board unfortunately have to make.'.

Rummenigge added that he did not think it was 'problematic' for these discussions to be happening publicly, due to the club's interest in 'him coming back and playing well'.

But the player union Fifpro were forthright in their disagreement with his statements,  releasing a statement claiming that all parties currently sharing their views on Musiala's contract 'should know better'.

'Bayern's honorary president, chief executive and former chief executive have all publicly questioned Musiala's contract in quick succession,' the statement read.

In a recent development, 'In Fifpro's view, this is a co-ordinated strategy to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives ahead of any negotiations. A club of Bayern's standing should know better.'.

When this statement was shared to social media via journalist Fabrizio Romano, global talents including Jude Bellingham and Musiala's team-mate Michael Olise were among those to like the post.

Musiala collapsed on the pitch at two consecutive games in August (pictured being helped by team-mates against RB Leipzig).

The 23-year-old has been diagnosed with absence seizures and is managing his medication.

Vincent Kompany has been supportive of his player's struggles, and took him off the bench with some success last weekend.

Rio Ferdinand elaborated on those comments in a more detailed post on social media, adding that he believed the club are 'better than this'.

Industry observers note that 'If they want to negotiate more reasonable terms for the club going forward due to the health issues Jamal has, then surely speak to him and his team rather than to the media,' Ferdinand wrote on X. 'This situation must be hard enough to deal with for Jamal without the media and club officials talking about it publicly.

Recent findings suggest that 'Bayern Munich are one of the clubs who from afar have always carried themselves with a class and standard that most have admired. Sadly, this just doesn't feel like Bayern Munich in this situation.'.

Criticisms were even more fiery in Germany, with the vice president of Germany's player union Michael Franz accusing the club of harassment.

It has been revealed that 'What the Bayern Munich officials are doing, and I don't mean Kompany and (Max) Eberl (director of sport), who have behaved impeccably, seems despicable to me,' Franz shared in an interview with Sport1. 'There is even something about it that resembles harassment.'.

Sources indicate that 'A footballer's level of performance can be discussed publicly, but it is not right to talk about his illness and the salary he receives in such circumstances. We must not forget that Jamal Musiala has done everything in his power to come back.'.

'Money has become more key than the person, and that is unacceptable.'.

Former Bayern captain Stefan Effenberg stressed how important 'support and protection' from the club towards their players is, particularly for those in greater need like Musiala.

Sources indicate that 'We are talking about someone who is suffering from an illness. What I would have expected is for the club's senior officials to apologise,' Effenberg said, adding that he thought that the communications from the club had been 'disastrous'.

Musiala collapsed twice within four days in mid-August, first during Bayern's match against Leipzig – shortly after scoring – and then against Heidenheim.

He then returned to the pitch in September, netting against Bodo/Glimt in Champions League action and Union Berlin shortly before the first international break.

After suffering a hamstring injury, Musiala then spent time away from the side before his return at the end of last week – a match which also saw Harry Kane suffer an ankle injury which will keep him out for over three months.

Fifpro's statement went on to add that Bayern must be careful with their player's mental wellbeing as well as his physical challenges.

Sources indicate that 'Bayern has a duty of care to Musiala,' the statement continued. 'Across professional football, uncertainty about a player's future can take a toll on their mental health, particularly when they are recovering from injury.

'Making Musiala's health and future a matter of public debate adds to that pressure. Any concerns about his contract should be raised privately with him and his representatives.

'Contracts are there to be respected. An injury or a dip in form gives a club no grounds to reopen terms it agreed to, just as a run of outstanding performances gives a player no automatic right to a pay rise.'.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s now coming up to six months since Arne Slot was relieved of his duties as Liverpool head coach after two years in the role.

The Dutchman had the unenviable task of succeeding Jurgen Klopp in the Anfield dugout but delivered a surprise (and emphatic) Premier League title triumph in his first season in charge before the Reds’ fortunes nosedived dramatically last term.

The 48-year-old just about managed to achieve Champions League qualification in May, but the extent of the decline from 12 months previously made his position untenable, and he was dismissed to make way for Andoni Iraola.

In his latest Liverpool Confidential feature for the Daily Mail, Lewis Steele addressed the question of what Slot has been getting up to since his exit from Anfield, with the journalist ‘often asked’ about the Dutch tactician’s more recent endeavours.

He outlined that the former Reds boss has been ‘biding his time and enjoying holidays with loved ones’, including multiple trips to Ibiza and taking in football matches in Argentina and Brazil with his son Joep, along with attending games in his native Netherlands.

The 48-year-old turned down the chance to coach his country after the World Cup, as well as potentially ‘lucrative gig’ in Saudi Arabia. He also declined approaches from a few clubs in the summer, including AC Milan, who now have ex-Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim in charge.

Steele concluded that Slot is ‘waiting for the right opportunity’ to get back into the dugout and doesn’t believe that his ‘stock has fallen’ as much as some of his peers who’ve been sacked by other high-profile Premier League clubs.

Sources indicate that want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

The Dutchman’s Liverpool tenure may have ended on a low ebb, and the prevailing sentiment in May was that the time was right for a change, but it’d be wrong to describe his two-year spell at Anfield as a failure.

He vastly exceeded expectations by winning the Premier League at the first attempt, and while last season was undoubtedly a massive underachievement results-wise, it must be viewed in the context of Slot and the squad trying to navigate the horrendous grief of Diogo Jota’s tragic death.

That the 48-year-old has turned down job approaches in order to hold out for the ‘right opportunity’ indicates his confidence that he’ll get back on board the managerial carousel sooner rather than later, and that his reputation hasn’t been overly tarnished by the disappointment of 2025/26.

Most Liverpool fans would also acknowledge that Slot carried himself with tremendous dignity throughout his time with us, striking the perfect tone with his farewell message to supporters after his sacking and – most importantly – handling the loss of Jota with commendable grace.

It’s nice to hear that the Dutchman has been enjoying his time with family since departing Merseyside, and it wouldn’t surprise us in the slightest if he were to be back in the technical area with a new club over the next few months.

Wherever his career might take him from here, we wish him the best in his future endeavours.

Latest Update: A disappointing end to a disappointing match for Newcastle United Women

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1418 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Coming into the Newcastle United Women game with Nottingham Forest, both sides knew they were already eliminated from the Subway Players cup, so it was perhaps always going to be something of a ‘Dead Rubber’.
  • But with an international break looming it was still a chance for some players to stake a claim for a starting berth when the action resumes.
  • In a recent development, forest made a raft of changes with Grace McEwen and Ebba Hed joining the ever-present Hannah Coan in central defence, with the trio forming a near impenetrable barrier.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Coming into the Newcastle United Women game with Nottingham Forest, both sides knew they were already eliminated from the Subway Players cup, so it was perhaps always going to be something of a ‘Dead Rubber’.

But with an international break looming it was still a chance for some players to stake a claim for a starting berth when the action resumes.

In a recent development, forest made a raft of changes with Grace McEwen and Ebba Hed joining the ever-present Hannah Coan in central defence, with the trio forming a near impenetrable barrier. Both Codie Thomas and the rapid Deanne Rose operated on the flanks to great effect and caused United problems throughout.

They went with a midfield three of Rachel Rowe sitting in front of the impressive and hard working pair Georgia Brougham and Tove Almsqvist. While Norwegian Tuva Espas and the on loan Lois Shooter partnered one another up front and looked lively.

Newcastle United Women made some subtle changes with Kayla Rendell coming back in goal, while Jemma Purfield returned to the back four. Mollie Lambert was given a chance to play in her favoured central midfield berth while Beth Lumsden shifted over to the left wing to accommodate Leanne Kiernan, who was starting against her former side.

Photo by Adam Mackman via The Mag.

Newcastle enjoyed the majority of the possession but clear cut chances were few and far between, with any opportunities that were created seemed to be snatched at or fired over the bar.

It has been revealed that the Lady Mags created a couple of opportunities early on, with Beth Lumsden and Lois Joel going close. Before Jordan Nobbs was denied by the impressive Hannah Coan inside the area with a crucial block. Nobbs had another chance soon after, but her effort from a tight angle out wide was claimed by Forest goalie Georgie Ferguson.

Forest were creating chances of their own though. Codie Thomas put the ball into the box from the left, but Tuva Espas was unable to steer her header on target. However, they were soon ahead and with it the game changed over a four minute passage of play.

Industry observers note that A speculative cross from Canadian international Deanne Rose out on the left was aimed at picking out Tove Almqvist but it flashed across goal and looked to be ushered out by Kayla Rendell. The goalie, on-loan from Manchester United, let the ball go past her as she assumed it was going wide of her far post, only to look foolish when the ball actually crept in off the woodwork.

According to recent reports, despite that setback Newcastle United Women responded well and from the ensuing kick-off were almost back level. Beth Lumsden playing on her less favoured left flank sent in a deep cross which was headed wide by Lambert.

But moments later Forest doubled their lead, when Tuva Espas forced a turnover in the United half and, spotting Rendell off her line, lobbed a perfect shot over the stranded goalie and into the net from 40 yards out.

Forest could have been three goals to the good before the break as Rachel Rowe worked the ball into the box, but was unable to find the final pass.

Sources indicate that newcastle had a lot of work to do in the second half but it was Forest who were looking the more dangerous side. Tove Almqvist played a ball over the Lasses defence as she tried to pick out Espas in the box, but Rendell was just able to gather it first.

Industry observers note that it perhaps should have been 3-0 to the East Midlands side when a brilliant move was started by captain Georgia Brougham. She played the ball into Rowe who in turn found Espas, with the Norwegian international able to advance down the right before sending a great ball in for her strike partner Lois Shooter. However, United captain Rachel McLauchlan got there first and sent her clearance onto the post and very nearly into her own net before it bounced clear to safety.

Forest continued to create chances after that. Rowe curled an effort from the edge of the area and Rose continued to be a nuisance on the wing as she carried the ball with confidence into the final third and won a free-kick. Then did excellently to keep hold of the ball before playing it into the centre circle, to substitute Aimee Claypole, but she sent her effort straight at Rendell.

Claypole, who was on loan at Durham a couple of seasons ago, missed another chance after Freya Thomas played the ball into her feet. Her effort took a deflection before being collected once again by Rendell. Rose had another chance in stoppage time but could only find the side netting.

It has been revealed that there were very few clear cut chances in the remainder of the game with Jordan Nobbs perhaps going closest when forcing Ferguson into a low save. Codie Thomas was also strong defensively and prevented another Newcastle shot. While Purfield fired over the bar from close range before sending a corner into Ferguson’s hands.

Sources indicate that on what was a frustrating day for Newcastle, one bright spark was the introduction of Jessie Gale who ran her socks off after coming on, putting the Forest backline under rare pressure. The youngster’s cross/shot forced Ferguson into a save to preserve her clean sheet.

With just seconds left of stoppage time frustration began to tell and when Lois Joel shot into the net after the referee blew his whistle she was shown a yellow card, which then turned to red for dissent.

A disappointing end to what was a disappointing day.

Newcastle United: Kayla Rendell, Rachel McLauchlan (c), Hanna Németh (Aoife Mannion 88), Jemma Purfield, Kaitlyn Torpey, Lois Joel, Mollie Lambert (Jessie Gale 54), Jordan Nobbs, Beth Lumsden (Emilia Larsson 67), Martha Thomas, Leanne Kiernan (Kathleen McGovern 54).

Subs not used: Anna Tamminen, Hildur Antonsdóttir, Oona Sevenius, Gemma Evans, Abbie Richardson.

Nottingham Forest: Georgie Ferguson, Codie Thomas, Grace McEwen, Hannah Coan, Ebba Hed (Abbie Lafayette 89), Deanne Rose, Georgia Brougham (Freya Thomas 72), Tove Almqvist (Cerys Brown 89), Rachel Rowe, Tuva Espas (Aimee Claypole 62), Lois Shooter (Shania Hayles 61).

Subs not used: Katie Cox, Lucy Carney, Melissa Johnson, Lily Stevenson.

Where that leaves Newcastle United Women.

Sources indicate that the League Cup has adopted a Swiss League format for fixtures, with only the top eight teams of 23 progressing to the quarter finals. Both Newcastle and Forest were already mathematically eliminated before this game so the result matters very little.

In a recent development, if you ignore the games played against WSL 1 sides Aston Villa and Everton, then Newcastle have conceded five goals in all competitions this season with four of those coming against Forest, who like United are still unbeaten in the league. That suggests the Lace City side should be one to look out for in the second half of the season, as along with Sunderland, they are the best side to face the Lady Mags so far.

A final concern was the standard of officiating for this game. With this being a clash between two second tier sides and a premier competition, surely the standard of the referee and assistants should be better than using ones from the local Non-League circuit. There are plenty of top female officials in the top tiers of the women’s game so surely both Newcastle and Forest deserved better? A referee who needlessly sent off a player in the 94th minute and his flag waving buddies who struggled to keep up with the play throughout the game, simply isn’t good enough.

Newcastle only have one WSL 2 game remaining before the Christmas break, against Watford on Sunday, 20th December.

There is now an international break before an FA Cup Third Round tie away to Manchester Unity on the 13th December with the host team based in Chadderton, Oldham. The Lasses faced the same opponents in the cup back in November 2023, winning 9-2 away from home on that occasion. But following the game both sets of fans developed a great likeness for one another with many Newcastle fans supporting Unity in their games over the past three years.

The following Wednesday sees Newcastle bring their League Cup campaign to a close with current leaders Manchester United set to visit St James’ Park for a rare midweek game under the floodlights.

Pregnancy rewires the brain — scientists are finally mapping it

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (881 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Researchers are striving to understand the massive changes in the brain that occur during pregnancy.Credit: Getty.
  • Sources indicate that pregnancy floods the brain with hormones and remodels brain circuits on a scale rivalled only by the neural transformation that occurs during adolescence.
  • Now, researchers are working to fill that void by collecting scans from first- and second-time mothers and analysing thousands of archived brain scans acquired during routine clinical care.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Researchers are striving to understand the massive changes in the brain that occur during pregnancy.Credit: Getty.

Sources indicate that pregnancy floods the brain with hormones and remodels brain circuits on a scale rivalled only by the neural transformation that occurs during adolescence. Yet there is a lack of information about how a healthy brain changes during pregnancy, because of past worries about the safety of scanning expectant mothers.

How pregnancy reshapes the brain throughout life.

How pregnancy reshapes the brain throughout life.

Now, researchers are working to fill that void by collecting scans from first- and second-time mothers and analysing thousands of archived brain scans acquired during routine clinical care. The work, presented on 17 November at the Society for Neuroscience annual meeting in Washington DC, could help to explain why some people develop depression during and after pregnancy, and how they develop other maternal mental-health conditions. These conditions are the leading driver of pregnancy-related deaths in the United States.

In a recent development, it wasn’t until 2024 that researchers reported the first detailed map of a human brain during pregnancy1, after performing magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) on one woman at 26 timepoints from 3 weeks before conception until 2 years after delivery. The American College of Radiology endorsed the safety of scanning the brains of pregnant people for research purposes that same year.

“Over 80% of women worldwide will experience pregnancy at least once in their lifetimes,” so it’s “imperative” that physicians spot signs of abnormalities early enough to treat conditions such as postpartum depression, stated Hannah Grotzinger, a cognitive neuroscientist at the University of Virginia in Charlottesville, during a presentation at the meeting. (Grotzinger was also a co-author of the 2024 study.).

Building on the earlier mapping study, Grotzinger and her colleagues expanded the effort to see whether those patterns hold across several people. They tracked six first-time mothers, two second-time mothers and five female participants who were not pregnant. From before conception to one year after birth, each participant underwent up to 30 MRI scans and blood draws.

It has been revealed that how does the brain react to birth control? A researcher scanned herself 75 times to find out.

Recent findings suggest that how does the brain react to birth control? A researcher scanned herself 75 times to find out.

Recent findings suggest that the larger cohort confirmed the shifts first seen in the 2024 map. In first-time mothers, total brain volume had dropped by roughly 3.5% by the time they gave birth. Grey-matter volume was reduced in nearly every region of the brain’s outer layer, or cortex, particularly in areas linked to social cognition. A brain structure called the pallidum, which regulates movement and motivation, was a rare exception: it grew during gestation, when a baby was growing in the womb. The researchers also found that the volume of cerebrospinal fluid, the liquid that surrounds and flows through the brain and spinal cord to provide cushioning and nutrients, increased by 11% during gestation.

It has been revealed that second-time mothers revealed a similar pattern, but across only about half of their cortical regions. There was no substantial shift in cerebrospinal-fluid volume, suggesting that a first pregnancy has a bigger impact on the brain, Grotzinger stated, although she cautioned that more data are needed to confirm these findings given the small sample size.

Such drastic changes to the brain are part of a typical pregnancy and are “not something to be scared of”, claims Liisa Galea, a neuroscientist at the Centre for Addiction and Mental Health in Toronto, Canada.

Recent findings suggest that the researchers also observed between the first and second trimester an increase in blood flow in the brain, which peaked around 21 weeks into pregnancy and tapered off near birth. The exception was a participant who developed pre-eclampsia, a serious pregnancy complication characterized by high blood pressure; the blood flow in their brain remained lower overall throughout gestation, compared with that in other participants, and they had less of a reduction in grey matter.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03804-7.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola has been provided with a timely team news boost ahead of the Premier League showdown against Manchester United on Sunday.

With the international break now concluded, the Reds players who were away with their countries have now reconvened on Merseyside and were put through their paces at the AXA Training Centre on Thursday.

There were no fresh injury concerns arising from national team duties, and there had already been good news earlier in the week when Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni resumed first-team training as they both close in on long-awaited returns from lengthy absences.

As per Liverpool Echo, a number of Reds players who had been carrying slight knocks or been absent through injury prior to the international window are now on course to be available for the Man United fixture.

The Dutch trio of Virgil van Dijk, Ryan Gravenberch and Jeremie Frimpong all trained, with the captain skipping Netherlands duty due to a minor concern, the midfielder missing our last three games with a heel problem, and the right-back overcoming a muscle injury he sustained in mid-October.

(Photo by Kate McShane/Getty Images).

Dominik Szoboszlai had played through a slight knee problem for Hungary in recent days, but he was involved in the session in Kirkby today, albeit with strapping on the affected area.

Two other notable inclusions were Alexis Mac Allister and Ronald Araujo, both of whom partook in training despite being just back from representing their countries in South America, although Bradley and Leoni weren’t involved in today’s session as their recoveries are being managed carefully.

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

Iraola will be delighted to get through the international window with no fresh injury absentees (unlike the damaging extended break earlier in the autumn), and also to see those who had been carrying knocks all involved in the session this morning.

The returns of Gravenberch and Frimpong give the head coach greater scope for selection in midfield and at right-back respectively, and Van Dijk and Szoboszlai could both be cleared to start as they seem to have shaken off their minor issues.

Barring any fresh setbacks between now and Sunday, it looks as though the only definite absentees for the Man United game will be Bradley, Leoni and Hugo Ekitike, each of whom continue to nurse long-term injuries but are on course to return in the coming weeks.

Sources indicate that iraola will inevitably be asked for updates on each of those players when he holds his pre-match press conference on Friday afternoon, and his squad seems to be nicely stocked at the beginning of what’ll be a punishing fixture schedule in the lead-up to the festive period. Long may it stay that way!

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Matthias Jaissle didn’t have the smoothest of arrivals at Newcastle United.
  • Disgruntled at him choosing to move on and United meeting his £9.5m release clause, Al Ahli delaying paperwork so he couldn’t start work with NUFC until only 18 days before the Premier League season kicked off.
  • A Newcastle United team that had finished 12th last season in the Premier League under an impossible 58 game schedule across all competitions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Matthias Jaissle didn’t have the smoothest of arrivals at Newcastle United.

Disgruntled at him choosing to move on and United meeting his £9.5m release clause, Al Ahli delaying paperwork so he couldn’t start work with NUFC until only 18 days before the Premier League season kicked off.

A Newcastle United team that had finished 12th last season in the Premier League under an impossible 58 game schedule across all competitions.

Coming in and inheriting a team that lost star players Tonali, Trippier, Gordon and Bruno this summer, then see a Sporting Director in control of a very defined focus on overwhelmingly recruiting younger players from overseas with the hope they will increase in quality and value across the coming years.

Fair to say this was always going to be a season of challenge for Matthias Jaissle.

Returning after the latest international break, the toughest possible matches awaited.

Reigning champions/current leaders Arsenal at St James’ Park, then away at Brighton, the only team to take any points off Arsenal in the opening ten rounds of Premier League matches.

Arsenal turned up on Saturday and did what they have done all season, they suffocated Newcastle United across the entire first half.

The Gunners passed and passed, The Magpies chased and chased.

Arsenal kept the ball, Newcastle couldn’t get it.

Matthias Jaissle’s team couldn’t get out of their own half and once the visitors took the lead, I would be surprised if any Newcastle United fan thought this would be anything other than a defeat.

In 14 Premier League and Champions League matches so far, Arsenal had won 12, lost that game at Brighton, plus drew 2-2 at Bayern Munich.

Apart from those Bayern and Brighton matches, Arsenal had conceded a grand total of three goals across the other 12 matches in the Champions League and Premier League, an average of a goal every 6+ hours in these dozen games.

According to recent reports, ahead of Saturday’s second half, Arsenal had Newcastle United right where they wanted them. Having dominated the opposition and taking the lead, if the home side came out and tried to get back into the game, gaps would open for the visitors to ruthlessly exploit. It is the Arsenal way.

The second half about to start and Matthias Jaissle surprises everybody, three subs at such an early stage. Jacob Ramsey, Anthony Elanga and Tino Livramento replacing Sean Steur, Jacob Murphy and Amar Dedic.

It has been revealed that from the first whistle of that second period it was Newcastle United on the front foot. Going toe to toe with Arsenal, or rather, stamping on their toes.

It was exhilarating, it was what we love to see, what we had seen so many times under Eddie Howe when up against Mikel Arteta. Only Matthias Jaissle having to do it with an admittedly lower quality team, no disrespect and all that.

However, those in black and white elevated themselves as a team, they were greater than the sum of their parts.

Whatever Matthias Jaissle had stated to them at the break, when added to the changes made, it was stunning.

Arsenal were clearly not expecting this in any way, United players flooding forward in such a brave high press. Joe Willock forced Martin Odegaard into losing possession, William Osula swept forward with the loose ball and a perfect pass for Harvey Barnes to do what Harvey Barnes does.

An equaliser four minutes into the second half, so sit back and defend a 1-1?

Matthias Jaissle ordering his team to get at Arsenal, drive them back, force errors, potentially more chances….

Just after the hour mark it is Tino Livramento of all people who forces a defender, then David Raya in his six yard box into mistakes that resulted in a corner.

A brilliant corner kick routine sees Arsenal out-Arsenaled, defenders blocked off and Dan Burn totally unmarked, his header parried but Joe Willock doing brilliantly to nudge the ball away from defenders despite pinned by opponents on the ground, on the line, Malick Thiaw smashing the ball home from a few inches out. Wow.

Sit back and try to defend a 2-1 for the next 37 minutes?

Matthias Jaissle insisting that his rejuvenated team keep taking the game to Arsenal.

It was 100% the correct approach.

Those remaining 37 minutes saw Newcastle United created more and better chances.

It has been revealed that arsenal scored a goal on the break which was brilliantly worked but still needed to go through a defender’s legs and a shot that Hornicek should probably have saved. That’s football.

Newcastle United didn’t take any of their chances and so it ended 2-2.

What a match and what an astonishing second half.

This was so so good from Matthias Jaissle.

The coward’s way would have been to approach the second half with a mentality of keeping it tight and running the clock down. Arsenal would have kept the ball for 90% of the time, happy to take a 1-0 or 2-0 win back to London, Newcastle would have been the victims of a predictable loss.

The minority of boo boys were vocal once again at half-time with United trailing to the champions/champions-elect.

By going for it after the break, Matthias Jaissle would have known Arsenal the massive favourites to get a second goal as gaps appeared and it could easily end a very messy three or four goal home defeat.

Yet he didn’t take the coward’s way, Matthias Jaissle went for it and Newcastle United (and their fans) got the reward.

This is the kind of manager I want.

He is for sure still learning the Premier League ropes but I think he has something about him.

Certainly enough to suggest that he deserves a proper fair chance.

The uber Matthias Jaissle critics say Newcastle United desperately need a Premier League proven manager. Rarely, if ever, do they ever name this mythical creature.

What exactly do they mean by Premier League proven? We aren’t getting Pep Guardiola or Jurgen Klopp!

What we would be getting is Premier League proven failures.

In a recent development, yes, let’s get Sean Dyche in. I can’t wait.

Recent findings suggest that yes, let’s get Rafa Benitez back and ruin all those great memories we have of how he stood by us at our moment of need. Rafa’s career has fallen off a cliff since NUFC and it would be horrific to see him come back and get abuse when he failed.

All managers have to start somewhere, only a very small handful of individuals who were stellar players then get gifted a top club in their first job as manager.

Matthias Jaissle has done well in Austria and Saudi Arabia.

Now he deserves a fair and proper chance in the Premier League, with Newcastle United.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The World Cup is set to return to America after FIFA awarded the 2031 women's tournament to a historic four-nation bid.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By ISABEL BALDWIN, US ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR.

Published: 10:23 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 13:19 EST, 23 November 2026.

The World Cup is set to return to America after FIFA awarded the 2031 women's tournament to a historic four-nation bid.

Following the success of the men's tournament this summer, the United States was unveiled as one of the hosts of the women's edition in five years' time during a virtual meeting of FIFA's national associations on Monday.

The US will co-host the global soccer extravaganza alongside Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica after the four countries' joint bid was awarded uncontested the 2031 tournament.

The selection marks a milestone for the Women's World Cup with the tournament being hosted across four nations for the first time in its history.

The last World Cup was co-hosted by multiple countries for the first time with the 2023 edition taking place across Australia and Latest Zealand.

This summer's men's World Cup was also co-hosted by the US with games taking place across the States, Canada and Mexico.

The World Cup is set to return to the United States for the 2031 women's edition of the event.

Spain are reigning champions after winning the Women's World Cup in 2023.

The United States Women's National Team are four-time winners in 1991, 1999, 2015 and 2019.

The 2031 tournament will also be the largest in the competition's history, featuring an expanded 48-team field and 104 matches for the first time.

'We are incredibly honored and excited to welcome the world to the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica for the 2031 FIFA Women's World Cup,' mentioned US Soccer President Cindy Parlow Cone.

Sources indicate that 'This is a historic moment for our four countries, but the opportunity is much bigger than any one of us. Together with FIFA, we want to deliver the biggest and most impactful Women's World Cup in history and use its success to accelerate the growth of women's soccer around the world. Our ambition is to create a tournament that not only inspires millions of players, but helps give them the opportunities to play, grow and pursue their dreams.'.

In a recent development, the selection marks the third time that the Women's World Cup has been awarded to the US with the country previously hosting the landmark 1999 and 2003 editions alone. The national team's tournament win in 1999 was the second of its four titles.

Meanwhile, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica will become first-time hosts at the historic tournament.

'This milestone furthers the continued belief that the best days of soccer in America are still ahead,' said U.S. Soccer CEO and General Secretary JT Batson.

It has been revealed that 'We have an opportunity to use the momentum from the 2031 FIFA Women's World Cup to accelerate our ambitions for the future of soccer, from expanding access and participation to strengthening the pathways that develop the next generation of players. We are excited to work alongside our partners across the region to make this tournament a defining moment for women's soccer.'.

The U.S.-led 2031 project across the CONCACAF regional soccer body bid offers FIFA a choice of stadiums in 20 cities: 14 in the U.S., four in Mexico plus San José in Costa Rica and Kingston, Jamaica.

US Soccer President Cindy Parlow Cone remarked the federation was honored to be selected.

The host selection of the 2035 Women's World Cup was awarded to a joint bid between England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales.

The host selection of the 2035 Women's World Cup was also announced on Monday with the tournament being awarded to another joint bid between England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales.

It marks the first time that a World Cup has been hosted on the British Isles since the men's tournament in 1966 in England.

The United Kingdom bid joins England with Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales that offers a choice from 19 venues, including Wembley Stadium in London.

The winning candidates and FIFA president Gianni Infantino promised commercially successful tournaments - the first editions with 48 teams and 104 games - and to reinvest all that money in women's soccer.

FIFA wanted these heavyweights of women's soccer to face no opposition without rival bids and so lead hosting the first expanded tournaments. That will bring parity with the men's World Cup which expanded to 48 teams this year in the US, Canada and Mexico.

The 2027 Women's World Cup will have 32 teams in Brazil.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Didi Hamann has been talking about Newcastle United.

Didi Hamann signed for Newcastle United in 1998 from Bayern Munich.

Kenny Dalglish the United manager who signed him for a reported £5.5m fee after the 1998 World Cup finals where he’d played for Germany.

Didi Hamann now giving his opinion on Newcastle United’s future stadium plans….

The former player turned pundit asked by Lottoland Live Casino: ‘Newcastle United are reportedly yet to decide whether to renovate or expand St James’ Park or build a completely new stadium. Do Newcastle United need a completely new stadium?’.

It has been revealed that didi Hamann replying: “No, no, you can’t leave St James’ Park. Obviously, I was fortunate and lucky to be able to play there for one season. I think it’s one of the best grounds in the league. With the extension they had, I think they get 51,000 [ED: 52k+ capacity now], and they probably can fit a few more in. If they can extend it, I think they’ve got to do everything to keep it. It’s right in the middle of the city. I think it’s one of the best, one of the most iconic stadia in the world. And I think this is why it would be majorly crucial to keep St James’. Don’t leave St James’ Park, please.”.

It is embarrassing that Didi Hamann is passing comment on this, considering how he was so desperate to leave St James’ Park less than a year after arriving and move to Liverpool.

The German international only started 20 Premier League matches for Newcastle United before forcing his way out of the club. In total he started 30 competitive games for United, plus one sub appearance. So fair to say he will have only started around 15 games in total at St James’ Park in a Newcastle United shirt.

The other thing when you are commenting on a club you don’t really care about, is that you also know precious little about the subject matter. If Didi Hamann had done his research then he would have known that there are zero plans to move the home of Newcastle United out of the city centre. That if indeed there is a new stadium built, then it will go up on a site no more than hundreds of yards away, very possibly even partly on the current St James’ Park site.

The former (very short-term!) United star also asked: ‘Newcastle and Liverpool are both known for their incredible atmospheres. Having played at both grounds, which stadium do you think has the better atmosphere and where did you enjoy playing more?’.

In a recent development, didi Hamann: “It’s very hard to compare because we didn’t play in Europe with Newcastle. Obviously, European nights at Anfield have always been special. But I’ve got to say, to walk out the first time at St James’ was just electric. When the music comes on, when you walk out and you see in my time, I think it was about 40, 45,000 Geordies [Ed: SJP capacity was 36k+ then] there. It was just fantastic. At the same time, I was in awe when I played with Newcastle the first time. I think it was Boxing Day that season in 1998 when we played Liverpool. When you stand in the tunnel there before it got redone. I think they are two of the best stadia in England. I’d go Premier League games at Newcastle, European nights at Anfield.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After another disastrous result last night, I was left scratching my head wondering what can actually be done to solve the problems facing West Ham. If results continue along this trajectory, the Hammers could find themselves looking nervously over their shoulders at the bottom end of the Championship table rather than fighting for promotion. At this rate, even a play-off spot feels optimistic.

I think 50 points might be enough to survive this league!

Earlier this week I wrote about the statistics, and they tell the real story behind West Ham’s struggles.

In a recent development, shot after shot, chance after chance, attack after attack, and still the ball refuses to go in. Remarkably, despite their wastefulness, the Hammers remain the division’s top scorers. In the last two matches alone, they have struck the woodwork five times.

Against Portsmouth, West Ham registered 19 shots with six on target and failed to score.

In a recent development, when you add that to the wider picture, the numbers become even more alarming. Across the last six matches, West Ham have taken 130 shots, with 41 on target, and scored only eight goals.

Sources indicate that at the opposite end of the pitch, defensive frailties and questionable goalkeeping continue to cost the team. Herrick was barely tested at Fratton Park, but when he was called into action, he was beaten. The goal will almost certainly be recorded as a goalkeeping error. Portsmouth created virtually nothing, yet their only shot on target produced the winning goal.

You can only work with the players available, but it’s difficult to understand how Areola has suffered multiple injuries this season despite not playing a competitive match. Entering the final year of his contract, albeit with a club option for an additional season, he is reportedly earning around £60,000 per week.

According to recent reports, these are concerns that might be understandable in the Premier League. This is the Championship. These players, including the youngsters, should be capable of performing consistently at this level.

Heads – down, negativity growing…time to stop the rot….

The negativity around the club is beginning to grow.

Sources indicate that nuno had to go, and he did. His departure gave Parker an opportunity to reintegrate certain players and rebuild fitness levels through competitive football. To be fair, time has not always been on the new manager’s side. However, following the international break, he has now had a chance to work with the squad, implement his ideas and stamp his authority on the team.

According to recent reports, the last two matches have to fall at his door. One point from six is simply not good enough. Extend that across his first four games and the record reads two defeats and two draws.

The much-talked-about newly introduced manager bounce? It never arrived.

In a recent development, you can see the frustration written all over the players’ faces. The supporters are becoming restless too, and I include myself in that group. I predicted a narrow 1-0 victory for West Ham at Portsmouth, but deep down I feared a repeat of the Preston performance. Unfortunately, those fears proved worse as at least we got a point on Saturday!

In a recent development, against Preston, West Ham enjoyed 80% possession and recorded 53 touches inside the opposition penalty area. Preston registered just ten.

At Fratton Park, the Hammers dominated possession with 63% of the ball and managed 29 touches in Portsmouth’s box compared to just eight for the home side.

Industry observers note that at this point, I’m running out of explanations. The statistics suggest West Ham should be winning games comfortably, but football is decided by goals, not data. Right now, the Hammers can’t convert their dominance into results, and until that changes, the gap between expectation and reality will continue to grow. I’m lost for words. I really am!

The Inbetweeners at Newcastle United, can they become success stories this series (this season) and beyond.

So much could depend on how this quarter perform.

Just in case you weren’t aware, The Inbetweeners is a brilliant (in my opinion anyway) comedy series (that has also then produced a couple of excellent films).

This comedy is the story of four teenagers who are misfits, neither totally cool nor total outcasts (hence The Inbetweeners), who regularly find themselves in awkward situations of their own making,.

This fictional quartet occasionally hint of moving on to a consistently successful level, but their own inherent frailties as well as outside factors, time after time conspire to prevent those glimpses of promise becoming ever more than that.

My focus isn’t on individuals who have just arrived this summer at St James’ Park, it isn’t on young players, it isn’t on older players where we pretty much know what we are going to get.

When it comes to The Inbetweeners at Newcastle United, I wanted to concentrate on this quartet below.

Four players who have played plenty of Premier League football in their careers and have shown enough to suggest they COULD be important, indeed vital, for Newcastle United this season.

All four of them also happen to play in the key midfield and attacking positions, the positions where United need far higher input and productivity if they are to create the chances and score the goals that can make the (positive) difference this season.

So without further ado, here are The Inbetweeners at St James’ Park:.

I think that arguably he is THE ultimate Inbetweener at Newcastle United. He was brilliant in that 2022-23 fourth place finish season before then serious injury hit then fitness and form concerns have followed.

At times we see THAT Joe Willock of 2022-23 and the second half on Saturday a prime example. Against his former club he was the key man in that second half,  the pressing of opposition players and his running with the ball, the Arsenal midfield couldn’t handle him at times. Willock pressured Odegaard into the mistake that produced the equaliser and then an assist for Thiaw’s strike.

Joe Willock would deserve to be first name on the team sheet if he consistently played like he did in that second half.

Started the season in electric form, confidence sky high as he scored within five minutes of the opening game against Liverpool, then in the first EPL away game scored a brilliant goal to set United on their way to beating Spurs.

Then injury hit and when he has returned, it feels a bit like Snakes and Ladders. He climbed plenty of ladders and got into a great position brimming with confidence, he then though hits one snake that sends his confidence and form sliding right back to rock bottom and needing to start again.

Industry observers note that I bit like Willock and Saturday’s second half, Elanga needs to simply get his head back in the place it was when Liverpool and Spurs couldn’t handle him. He is capable of being a huge player for Matthias Jaissle AND he needs to be that player to solve our problem on the right. He did alright on Saturday when he came on and maybe a huge factor can be if Tino Livramento now can stay fit as well on that side.

Very similar story to Anthony Elanga, started this season on fire and then lost his way.

According to recent reports, in certain moments, Yoane Wissa has looked unplayable (in a good way!) this season, some of his runs on the ball have been exhilarating. The one he made with a handful of Liverpool players challenging him half the length of the pitch before passing to Joe Willock for his goal, where has that gone?

Again like Elanga, with Wissa it feels like it is very much a confidence thing.

Recent findings suggest that he had an astonishing record at Brentford but I do feel he is an attacker who is more of a team player, he needs those around him also playing well. Hopefully if the team overall can become more consistent and then Yoane Wissa finds within that some special moments of his own, we can just maybe have that opening of this season player back again.

Of this quartet of Inbetweeners at Newcastle United, I think Ramsey deserves to be cut the most slack.

The former Villa star has still only started 15 Premier League matches for Newcastle United and was very unlucky with a bad early injury last season (thanks to Sean Longstaff) and desperately needs a run in the team to get his rhythm after having his own struggles with fitness and form.

Recent findings suggest that like the other three above, Jacob Ramsey has had moments where we can see the player Eddie Howe signed. The same as Joe Willock, Ramsey is very mobile, runs well with the ball, can be very effective with a high press, can be a difference maker.

According to recent reports, the second half on Saturday he showed that and I do think that if Newcastle United are to exceed any current expectations, we need to have players with pace who can swiftly carry the ball in transition an cause problems for opposition teams on a regular basis. If Jacob Ramsey and Joe Willock can do it against the best team in the country, admittedly just for one half on Saturday, why can’t they do it against the rest?

Once again though, the same as Yoane Wissa and Anthony Elanga, it is all about this quarter losing their status as The Inbetweeners at Newcastle United and proving to be something far better than that.

Here’s hoping they prove they are worthy of another series.

Two more Liverpool fixtures in the Premier League have been rescheduled for live TV coverage, as confirmed on Thursday.

With the November international break now concluded, the Reds’ next couple of domestic fixtures are against Manchester United and Everton, with the reverse of those games against our two biggest traditional rivals taking place on consecutive weekends in January.

The fixture list for the remainder of this year had already been locked in, and the first month of 2027 has now been set, other than prospective FA Cup and Carabao Cup matches.

On Thursday, the Premier League announced updated dates and times for matches in January, with two of Liverpool’s games being moved.

The home clash against Crystal Palace remains a 3pm kick-off on Saturday 16th, but the subsequent two games have unsurprisingly been chosen for TV coverage.

The Reds will now face Manchester United at Old Trafford on Sunday 24 January at 4:30pm (live on Sky Sports), with the Merseyside derby at Anfield taking place six days later with a 12:30pm kick-off (live on TNT Sports).

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

The new dates and times for the Man United and Everton games have left Liverpool with a rather difficult week towards the end of January.

Just three days after the game at Old Trafford, the Reds have their concluding fixture in the league phase of the Champions League at home to Lens, and then a turnaround of just over 50 hours to hosting the Toffees at Anfield.

*FA Cup third round draw and fixture details to be confirmed in December.

**If Liverpool advance to Carabao Cup semi-finals.

The hope is that, by the time the Ligue 1 outfit visit L4 on 27 January, we’ll already be assured of a direct passage to the round of 16 and there won’t be anything riding on that game for Andoni Iraola’s side.

Liverpool at the moment have seven matches in the diary in the first month of 2027, with an FA Cup third-round tie to be added for the weekend of 9/10 January and a potential Carabao Cup semi-final first leg in the subsequent midweek, should we defeat Bournemouth at Anfield next month.

It’s quite plausible that the Reds could have two matches against Everton in January, with both teams still in the Carabao Cup and favourites to win their respective quarter-finals (the Toffees are away to Fleetwood of League Two).

Three Merseyside derbies in the first five weeks of 2027 would be the definition of familiarity breeding contempt, but for now the sole focus for Iraola and co is the small matter of Man United at home on Sunday.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With only two points from his first four games, West Ham manager Scott Parker is already coming under pressure, with some even questioning whether he is the right man to take the club forward following last night’s defeat at Portsmouth.

Sources indicate that for me, it’s a little premature to be discussing the fresh manager’s job security. But make no mistake about it, West Ham are a club in crisis, and there is a lot more wrong than just the manager.

However, the one thing Parker can control is how he utilises the players at his disposal. And from my seat in Row B at Fratton Park, it was evident that Parker appears no closer to knowing what his best starting XI is.

Issues in both full-back positions, a lack of creativity through the middle, genuine issues on the left wing and three strikers who can’t score goals.

Industry observers note that west Ham huffed and puffed against Pompey, and no doubt the statistics will have been boosted by a late flurry towards the end of the game when we battered the Portsmouth goal for five minutes. But that could not disguise the fact that we were watching a very, very poor West Ham team.

I had a close-up view of West Ham hams problems from row B at Fratton Park.

Possibly the most disturbing aspect is that neither Preston North End nor Portsmouth, in our last two games, have looked like particularly good teams. The fact of the matter is that you don’t have to be a decent side to beat West Ham.

We now find ourselves closer to the relegation places than automatic promotion, and I’ve seen little to suggest that anyone knows how to turn us around and get us pointing in the right direction.

There’s a big game coming up at the London Stadium against Stoke City, but make no mistake about it, the Potters will be licking their lips at the prospect of turning over West Ham.

The Hammers are now starting to look less like promotion certainties and more like Leicester City.

Even with former Hammers legend Mark Noble on the coaching staff, the players look lost and at times without fight or character. Which comes as a shock to supporters who had expected the opposite would be the case with the hugely popular duo at the helm.

Noble and Parker have to pick the eleven who will try their hearts out and run over hot coals for their manager and their supporters.

At least then the players won’t hang back for fear of being abused amidst away-end ‘ugly scenes‘ after the final whistle as the BBC reported.

On the face of it West Ham have too few options in key areas of the pitch, meaning that despite their ineffectiveness, the same payers have to be utilised again and again.

So Piroe’s ineffectiveness is set to continue.

The same applies in the case of  right back Joel Veltman: Albeit through Kyle Walker Peters‘ injury, Scott Parker has very little option but to start the Dutchman again, despite his pretty universally condemned performance at Fratton Park.

Veltman- unable to add much to West Ham’s offensive capabilities.

Footballfancast.com  single out Veltman for special mention:.

“The Dutchman, who is averaging 0.5 key passes and 0.1 dribbles per game, was once again ineffective in possession against Portsmouth before being substituted in the 62nd minute.

Veltman has never produced more than three assists in a season in his career and has not assisted more than one league goal in a season since the 2016/17 campaign with Ajax, which shows that he is an even bigger problem [than Piroe] as he does not have relevant experience to suggest that he will turn things around.

Parker must, now, drop the defender to the bench to explore his options in that area of the pitch, as the Hammers need more on the ball from the player in that position moving forward.”.

Sources indicate that can’t really argue with that but unless Scott Parker is prepared to start Arne Engels as an emergency right back then the Hammers boss is fresh out of options until Walker Peters recovers. Veltman was the free signing designed to give West Ham cover in the event of injury. We’d not perhaps envisaged him being required to play week in, week out. His failure going forward is likely the reason Jarrod Bowen is having to play so wide.

Just an observation but does seem a trend when Walker Peters is absent, that Bowen hugs the touch line more, knowing his full back is not going to overlap or assist him in the way in which Walker Peters can.

Time, then, for anxious glances to the treatment table to see how Walker Peter’s recuperation from his thigh muscle matter is going.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Graham Scott has been quizzed by an Arsenal fan as to why Malick Thiaw’s goal was allowed to stand on Saturday.

That goal put Newcastle United 2-1 up on 62 minutes.

Graham Scott refereed in the Premier League for a decade and he was also a video assistant referee (VAR) more than 100 times.

Now retired, he brings his unique insight into how match officials operate for The Athletic.

They invite readers to send in questions each week for Graham Scott to answer.

This week the former top referee received this one from an Arsenal fan….

‘Why did neither the referee nor VAR penalise the holding on Jurrien Timber that allowed Dan Burn to win a free header to create Newcastle’s second goal against Arsenal?’.

Graham Scott explaining: “Timber was impeded by Will Osula as he chased after Burn (circled below). Osula was impeded by Declan Rice, who was holding him with both arms. Malick Thiaw was being held by Martin Odegaard, who was being held by Thiaw. Lewis Miley blocked Ezri Konsa, who pulled Miley to get past him. There were probably other potential fouls, too. The officials look for the most serious offences that have the greatest impact, and none of these came close to meeting those thresholds — which are set by the league and the lawmakers, not the refs.”.

I know that no football fan takes it well when any decision goes against them BUT as a group I think Arsenal fans do appear especially bizarre in terms of not willing to accept any decision that doesn’t go their way.

Graham Scott was also asked another question regarding Saturday’s game….

Industry observers note that ‘When David Raya went down for treatment the first time at Newcastle on Saturday, why did another Arsenal player not have to leave the field for a minute? I thought that was the upcoming rule.’.

Graham Scott: ‘No Arsenal player was asked to leave the field for a minute because Raya had collided with an opponent and requested treatment at the earliest opportunity. There is a similar exemption if a goalkeeper’s injury occurs from a foul that the referee deems worthy of a yellow or red card. This rule was introduced to stop goalkeepers mysteriously sitting down and demanding treatment for fictitious muscle injuries while their coach held an impromptu time-out chat with the rest of the team.’.

According to recent reports, I have to confess, I totally forgot about this latest rule coming in. Has any goalkeeper got ‘injured’ this season and had treatment on the pitch which led to his Premier League side going down to ten men for a minute with an outfield player going off?

Aberdeen  boss Mario Frick has vowed to go on the attack when his new-look team take on Rangers at Ibrox tomorrow night.

Renowned for a high-octane attacking style of play at his previous clubs, the 52-year-old Liechtensteiner has already generated a wave of positivity at Pittodrie.

Aberdeen will face a tough task against an in-form Rangers side who are unbeaten in their last 13 matches.

But Frick insists there is no prospect of his team turning up at Ibrox and parking the bus in their efforts to take a positive result.

Industry observers note that 'I'm looking forward to it and I'm pretty confident in our squad,' he stated. 'Now we have to prove that and have another good performance.

'That's not our style (to sit in and defend). We want to play like we did at Kilmarnock. That's our style of play.

Frick is all smiles after his side put four goals past Kilmarnock in his first match in charge.

According to recent reports, 'Rangers will be a tough game. They are very strong, especially at home. I saw a lot of quality, particularly in their forward areas.

'I think, in the end, it was a deserved win and now we're looking forward to meeting Rangers at Ibrox.

According to recent reports, 'Defensively, we have to improve. Otherwise, it will be very difficult. I'm pretty sure we can defend better.

Industry observers note that 'But, like I say, we want to play like we did at the weekend. It's not our style (just to sit back and defend).'.

Kevin Nisbet is mobbed by team-mates after netting the first of his double at Rugby Park.

After the doom and gloom of the Stephen Robinson era, Frick has immediately created a feelgood factor at Aberdeen.

The fans were singing his name after the victory at Rugby Park on Saturday - and he wants to strengthen that feeling of unity throughout the club.

'It's been very good so far, especially with the win,' he added. 'The team has some confidence now and I see many players laughing.

It could not have come at a worse time for them and for the Premier League, and for the fans of every other club who wanted to see City humbled. On the pitch.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Breaking news on Wednesday that the Saudi Arabia PIF have put 25 per cent of Newcastle United up for sale.
  • The exclusive comes from David Ornstein and Chris Waugh at The Athletic.
  • They reveal that this would be done through the issuing of newly introduced shares.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Breaking news on Wednesday that the Saudi Arabia PIF have put 25 per cent of Newcastle United up for sale.

The exclusive comes from David Ornstein and Chris Waugh at The Athletic.

They reveal that this would be done through the issuing of newly introduced shares.

The Athletic stating: ‘The proposed transaction would see upcoming investors inject funds directly into the club, receiving up to a quarter shareholding in exchange. No funds would flow to PIF, but its existing stake would be diluted by the share glitch.’.

They add that JP Morgan (the Upcoming York City-headquartered global bank) has been appointed advisors and that the process to find investment is under way.

The Athletic journalists detailing: ‘Sources with knowledge of the situation, speaking on the condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to do so publicly, insisted that, at this point, a minority investor is being sought with PIF eager to raise money, in part to fund major infrastructure projects, and regard the issuing of fresh shares as a good means of doing so.’.

It appears that the 25 per cent of the total shareholding to be sold will come from the 84 per cent of the club owned by the Saudi Arabia PIF, as the report adds that: ‘The British Reuben family owns the remaining 16 per cent shareholding and Jamie Reuben is their representative on the board.’.

Back in May 2026, The Athletic had previously reported that the Newcastle United majority owners were open to selling a minority stake to help fund significant infrastructure projects: ‘However, people familiar with the matter insisted PIF retained a long-term commitment to the club they jointly bought from Mike Ashley for a total of £305million ($400.1m at present exchange rates) in 2021, though they were willing to dilute their shareholding and had already been approached by possible investors. Yasir Al-Rumayyan, PIF’s governor and Newcastle’s chairman, attended his first match of the season at St James’ Park on Saturday, watching Newcastle draw 2-2 with league champions Arsenal. Jamie Reuben was also at the match.’.

This news today hopefully signals a latest stadium will go ahead, as well as the state of the art training ground.

The Athletic adding: ‘While PIF was never going to pay for a fresh stadium outright — Newcastle have always been viewed as a long-term investment intended to bring them an eventual profit — any project of that scale would require a notable injection of equity as well as outside financing.’.

  • The Bundesliga teenager is high up on the list at German giants Bayern Munich, with the Bavarians expected to face competition from Bayer Leverkusen for his signature.
  • The attacking midfielder has registered four goal contributions in 11 games (across all competitions) this season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Liverpool are reportedly showing ‘concrete interest’ in highly-rated Gladbach talent Wael Mohya.

The Bundesliga teenager is high up on the list at German giants Bayern Munich, with the Bavarians expected to face competition from Bayer Leverkusen for his signature.

The attacking midfielder has registered four goal contributions in 11 games (across all competitions) this season.

Industry observers note that christian Falk told CF Bayern Insider: “However, Bayern Munich definitely have him on the list. And we should note that both Liverpool and Brighton in the Premier League are showing concrete interest in the 17-year-old attacking talent.

“This is why Gladbach would be well-advised to try and offer him a upcoming contract; that way, they can have some influence over how long the player stays at the club, or, at the very least, ensure that they get a sizeable sum from a permanent transfer.

“I heard that there has already been contact with Mohya’s agent, Thies Bliemeister, and they talked about a move to Leverkusen. The next step is to talk to the player, his family and then the club. He doesn’t have a long-term contract at Gladbach, so there is a chance to make this deal happen.”.

With a contract right now set to expire in the summer of 2028, Mohya represents a genuine market opportunity for clubs looking to invest in a high-potential option.

On that note, Brighton makes a great deal of sense as the next stop in the 17-year-old’s career (if not his final destination), similarly to Leverkusen in the German top-flight.

In a recent development, liverpool, it has to be remarked, would benefit greatly from a player with the Gladbach star’s profile, given they lack a viable backup option to Florian Wirtz in the ten position. Not to mention the fact that the footballer would provide further reassurance on the flanks.

Falk went on to add: “The 17-year-old was invited to the national team by Klopp during the international break. He wasn’t officially part of the squad; it was more just to give the player a taste of what international football looks like. He’s not totally clear yet about where he wants to commit, but Germany is putting up a strong fight to ensure that he pledges his international future to Die Nationalelf.”.

The major glitch facing Mohya in the coming weeks and months, of course, is whether a move to the likes of FC Bayern and Liverpool are actually in his best interest at this stage in his career.

Bayern Munich have Ismael Saibari and Jamal Musiala behind Harry Kane, albeit there are question marks over the latter’s long-term future in Munich in light of ongoing concerns over his health.

The Reds, of course, have Wirtz, in whom they invested a British transfer record fee (the total package being worth £116.5m). He’s played a significant percentage of the total minutes on offer in 2026/27 under new boss Andoni Iraola, and at 23 years of age, he’s hardly at any risk of sinking past his peak in the near future.

We’ve no doubt Liverpool would welcome having a rotational option of Mohya’s quality, whom they could develop on their own time, and they can supply evidence of how well they’re managing Rio Ngumoha’s development despite the presence of more senior figures in Bradley Barcola and Cody Gakpo.

But if Wael Mohya’s looking for an absolute guarantee of regular minutes, you could forgive him for either staying put in Germany or joining the talent factory line in Brighton.

For West Ham, Heaven represents an opportunity to add a highly rated young defender to a squad looking to strengthen after a difficult campaign…For West Ham, a loan agreement could offer an opportunity to give Heaven regular senior football without requiring a major permanent investment immediately.

His development at the club could then determine whether a longer-term deal becomes realistic.”.

#118297. Aston Villa and Newcastle United restricting competition parallels are now impossible to ignore
