Aston Villa and Newcastle United restricting competition parallels are now impossible to ignore

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1533 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Aston Villa and Newcastle United, two clubs with plenty in common.
  • Newcastle United winning a first major trophy in decades in 2025.
  • Aston Villa winning a first major trophy in decades in 2026.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Aston Villa and Newcastle United, two clubs with plenty in common.

Certainly in recent years anyway.

Newcastle United winning a first major trophy in decades in 2025.

Aston Villa winning a first major trophy in decades in 2026.

In recent years Newcastle United getting into the Champions League not once, but twice, for the first time in decades.

In recent years Aston Villa getting into the Champions League not once, but twice, for the first time in decades (since the days it was called the European Cup).

The two clubs with proud histories also have another far bigger thing in common.

They are by far and away the two disruptor Premier League clubs, the pair who have tried hardest to break the modern day ‘Massive Six’ financial stranglehold on long-term power and success.

Industry observers note that aston Villa and Newcastle United have flown closest to the Sun and suffered because of it, with UEFA SCR restrictions battering them into submission. If you don’t follow their warnings and get back in financial check, then face a ban from the Champions League (and other UEFA competitions) in the future.

It is all part of the endless vicious circle for clubs such as Aston Villa and Newcastle United who are attempting to narrow that yawning financial chasm that exists between themselves and the ‘Premier League Big Six’ who have been allowed to build such seemingly unchallengeable financial powerhouses across many years when Mike Ashley ran United into the ground and Villa suffered in many ways of their own.

This is the Champions League story of recent years for Aston Villa and Newcastle United.

2022-23 season Newcastle United qualify for next season’s Champions League but Aston Villa don’t.

Sources indicate that 2023-24 season Newcastle United compete in that season’s Champions League but Aston Villa don’t. Aston Villa qualify for next season’s Champions League but Newcastle United don’t.

In a recent development, 2024-25 season Aston Villa compete in that season’s Champions League but Newcastle United don’t. Newcastle United qualify for next season’s Champions League but Aston Villa don’t.

It has been revealed that 2025-26 season Newcastle United compete in that season’s Champions League but Aston Villa don’t. Aston Villa qualify for next season’s Champions League but Newcastle United don’t.

2026-27 season Aston Villa compete in that season’s Champions League but Newcastle United don’t. Qualifying for…Aston Villa??? Newcastle United???

Sources indicate that 2026-27 season Competing/Qualifying for…Aston Villa??? Newcastle United???

The pattern couldn’t be clearer for Aston Villa and Newcastle United in recent years.

An ability every other year to qualify for the Champions League BUT in years when playing in the top European competition, unable to also qualify for the following season’s Champions League.

In a recent development, four seasons in a row we have had either Newcastle United or Aston Villa disrupting the route of Premier League Major Six clubs to the Champions League BUT from where I am standing, it looks like that run is going to end now. I find it very unlikely that either Aston Villa or Newcastle United will qualify via the Premier League.

I think that now things have well and truly caught up with the two clubs and their ambitions.

I think to properly stand a chance of having a season where you can compete in the Champions League and attempt to qualify via the Premier League for the following season’s UCL competition, you need to have a squad with enough quality and depth to cope.

The financial rules make this all but impossible for Aston Villa and Newcastle United as things stand.

Industry observers note that wages are the most crippling thing, the Premier League Massive Six are able to pay far bigger wages than Newcastle United and Aston Villa. It reaches a point where they can’t pay their star plays anything close to the market rate (what they can get elsewhere). It also means that to try and somehow have a large enough squad to cope with both Premier League and Champions League, you need to sells some/all of your best players so you can afford to bring in enough signings to try and give you the depth.

The reality in recent years when Aston Villa and Newcastle United have been trying to do both, compete in the Champions League AND qualify for next season’s, they have to play their small group of very best players far too often. This all but guarantees these star players will pick up injuries and/or get fatigued and their effectiveness is vastly diminished.

Photo by Jamie Smith via The Mag.

I think the perfect storm has now arrived.

All of the above challenges have been impacted by the Premier League PSR and now SCR restrictions BUT even more so by the far stricter UEFA SCR restrictions on allowed spending on transfer fees and wages as a proportion of your revenues (UEFA allows 70% of ‘Adjusted operating revenue’).

I know that as football fans (especially those of Newcastle United and Aston Villa) we are heartily sick of all the accountancy boring side of things and how it constantly impacts the coverage of Premier League clubs these days.

To simply spell it out though, it basically means that if your revenues are twice as major as another club’s, you can spend twice as much on wages and transfer fees.

Roughly speaking, the likes of Arsenal, Liverpool, Man City and Man U have twice as big revenues as Aston Villa and Newcastle United have per season, whilst Chelsea and Tottenham are also way ahead AND have various other elements that give them an inbuilt advantage, which has been put in place across many years.

This past summer transfer window, in order to comply with UEFA SCR restrictions and avoid a future ban on taking part in UEFA competitions, both Villa and Newcastle had to take drastic action when it came to buying and selling players AND their wage bills.

It would have been unrealistic and reckless this summer for a club like Villa or Newcastle to agree to long-term huge wages of a level that ‘Major Six’ clubs can comfortably afford.

According to recent reports, you then have Newcastle United and Aston Villa also having to sell at least some of their best players because they generally bring in the biggest instant benefit to a club’s accounts. The transfer fee agreed (less the player’s current book value) all goes into that current season’s accounts as a profit. However, when a player is bought the transfer fee that is agreed is spread over the length of his contract, when it comes to showing as a cost in the annual accounts. So if you sign a player for £50m on a five year contract, each season it reveals as a £10m cost in the accounts. So basically if you sell a player for a big transfer fee it can help you afford a number of players for a total higher than that transfer fee BUT they still eventually have to be accounted for. Plus of course all Premier League clubs are constantly having those annual transfer fee costs for previous signings going into the accounts.

So what did Aston Villa and Newcastle United do in summer 2026?

Or rather, what did they HAVE to do?

Sources indicate that they both sold a lot of their best and highest paid players to other clubs. In general, these players went to clubs who paid them far higher wages. Then Villa and Newcastle generally recruited players on lower transfer fees, many of who they also hope will improve in terms of value as well as ability in years to come.

Newcastle United lost the likes of Gordon, Trippier, Bruno and Tonali, having previously had to sell Isak and sacrifice Minteh and Anderson as well.

As well as previous players they had been forced to trade, this summer Aston Villa moved on the likes of Rogers, Watkins, Martinez, Digne, Konsa and Tielemans.

Interesting to see where many of these players are now at:.

Bruno (Arsenal), Rogers (Chelsea), Isak (Liverpool), Tielemans (Man U), Tonali (Tottenham), Martinez (Chelsea), Anderson (Man City), Konsa (Arsenal)….

So not only are Aston Villa and Newcastle United forced to move on many of their best players in order to stay inside the UEFA and EPL SCR restrictions, they then see most of them end up at the very Premier League Massive Six clubs that they are trying to compete with, against the odds.

When it comes to power and success long-term, it feels very much like tossing a coin and it is heads the Premier League Big Six win, whilst tails sees Villa and Newcastle lose.

Aston Villa and Newcastle United presently sit 12th and 13th in the Premier League table, from 11 attempts each they have won three EPL matches apiece.

Where might the pair have been instead if the financial restrictions didn’t leave them hamstrung?

What if they weren’t prevented from matching the wages that Premier League Substantial Six clubs are able to pay, were able to keep all of their best players AND bring in similar quality ones that would help persuade them to stay AND enable them to properly compete long-term?

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Watching last night’s woeful performance against Portsmouth unfold, I was struck by the similarity in playing style of one current West Ham winger with a previous playing enigma from whom West Ham could never seem to coax the best.

Triggered by the  irritation generated from watching Manor Solomon constantly check back, slow down play and then inevitably cut inside, I found myself comparing him with another West Ham winger who repeated the same trick ad nauseam.

Even on the one occasion when he was put clean through beyond his full back, by a brilliant pass from Ezra Mayers, Solomon got to the by line and – infuriatingly, checked back instead of trying to cross with his weaker foot.

And at that moment I thought “Saïd Benrahma” all over again.

The enigma that was Saîd Benrahma: at least he scored a few, created a few, and smacked a mean penalty past Fiorentina’s keeper in the summer of 2023.

‘Benny’ could at least create chances (and score a mean penalty) whereas Manor Solomon just runs down blind alleys, head down, inevitably slowing and cutting inside to use his right foot.

Exactly as, on numerous occasions in each game, the Algerian would check back, infuriatingly, and slow up play instead of pressing on to beat his full back on the inside or out. In that respect Solomon seems identical, disrupting West Ham’s flow, allowing defenders to reset and frustrating the bejesus out of supporters.

At least Benrahma could create and occasionally score: Solomon has, by the reckoning of westhamworld.co.uk, now played “1141 minutes for two goals and two assists, averaging a goal every 285 minutes”.

For whatever reason the Israeli clearly is a shadow of the player who helped fire Leeds to promotion and West Ham need to consign him to the same ‘rest and recuperation’ home in which Mads Hermansen has been sent to recapture his form.

Austbo at least has a shot on him and seems to be able to beat players inside and out: With the Norwegian there is the feeling that there’s more to come. With Solomon, exactly as Tottenham fans suggested, the fear is that his best days are long in the rear view mirror. Much like Saîd Benrahma, but without the trophy to show for it.

News on Wednesday of a latest £375million cash injection targeted to help fund new Newcastle United stadium.

This comes with NUFC fans still waiting to hear definitive official confirmation of what is going to happen regarding stadium plans.

Earlier today The Athletic revealed that the Saudi Arabia PIF are willing to sell 25 per cent of the club, from their 84 percent majority ownership of Newcastle United.

Now The Mail report that their inside sources have told them that ‘This is not a case of Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund looking to sell the club, but rather by creating new shares…’.

They say that the club’s owners are now getting close to confirming their prepares for a latest Newcastle United stadium AND that today’s exclusive from The Athletic ties in with that.

The Mail stating that the sale of up to a quarter of the total shares in NUFC by Saudi Arabia PIF ‘Would be to inject upcoming equity to help fund infrastructural developments, including a stadium. With Newcastle mentioned to be valued at £1.5billion, this could equate to a £375million cash injection. PIF would retain their majority ownership…As one source said: ‘This is not about taking cash off the table, it is about funding growth.’.

JP Morgan have now been appointed as advisers in selling part of the Saudi Arabia PIF stake in the club, with The Mail saying that fellow Wall Street firm are also involved, with their role ‘…set to be to provide a loan or other investment to help finance the stadium. As we reported last week, the cost of a fresh home would not be exclusively funded by PIF and co-owner Jamie Reuben, with loans, share issues and investments all part of the package. The expectation is that a new stadium, rather than a St James’ renovation, will soon be recommended to the club’s owners by the executive team. It will then be up to PIF to sign off on the looks and for a public announcement to be prepared.’.

  • For anyone who witnessed the shambolic showing at Fratton Park on Tuesday night, that nightmare scenario suddenly doesn’t look so  ridiculous.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sure it couldn’t happen, could it? Only five times in the history of the Premier League have sides suffered successive relegations from the top tier to the third.

For anyone who witnessed the shambolic showing at Fratton Park on Tuesday night, that nightmare scenario suddenly doesn’t look so  ridiculous. West Ham in the third division, 62,500 seater stadium and all?

Alarming parallels exist between West Ham’s performance this season and that of their former competitors Leicester City who now find themselves playing their football in the third division.

According to recent reports, the Hammers are now in the bottom half of the Championship, with just 24 points from 17 games. At the same stage last season, the Foxes themselves, after 17 games had amassed … Exactly the same number of points.

All of which seemed unimaginable when the Irons beat Swansea five weeks ago to go second, and Nuno Espirito Santo picked upthe September manager of the month award.

Sources indicate that fratton Park showing was a real wake up call to West Ham’s management and board. This ship is sinking.

Industry observers note that the only positive is that a month is a long time in this league. A run of form could be just around the corner and any team – West Ham included – can win five or six games and transform their fortunes. But the Hammers’ form at present is most definitely that of a relegation candidate rather than a play-off hopeful.

Which hardly helps the recruitment in January.

For anyone living under the misconception that Leicester City’s case was an isolated example and that lightning couldn’t strike twice, Wolverhampton Wanderers, who were also relegated in 2012/13, had 22 points after 17 games.

Stoke City come calling on Saturday with a seriously impressive run of form, unbeaten in six whereas the Hammers are winless in their last half dozen. No time like the present to get back to winning ways and arrest the downhill slide. One relegation is enough, thank you very much.

The home side go into the fixture 10 points and 14 places ahead of their arch-rivals, for whom this is a first game in charge for upcoming head coach Mauricio Pochettino.

The Reds’ home record in the Premier League so far this season has been poor, with just one win from five, but victory today would see them close to within one point of third-placed Manchester City.

In his weekly Premier League column for BBC Sport, Sutton voiced his belief that the visitors won’t have any ‘latest manager bounce’ at Anfield and has forecast Liverpool to win handsomely.

The former Chelsea striker wrote: ‘Liverpool are still a work in progress, and United have picked up some results at Anfield recently – two draws and a win in their past three visits – but I can only see one result here, and it is a home victory.

In a recent development, ‘Pochettino will probably look to defend and play on the counterattack, and they might get some chances that way, but Liverpool are going to win. The only question is how many they will score.

Sources indicate that ‘Carrick began by beating Manchester City and Arsenal in his first two games in January. Pochettino might start by being on the wrong end of a pummelling.’.

Sutton has predicted a resounding 4-0 win for Liverpool, matching the scoreline from this fixture in April 2022.

According to recent reports, want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

Considering the form and league positions of the teams, objectively the Reds ought to go into this game as clear favourites. When fifth plays host to second from bottom in the Premier League, the former would naturally be expected to win.

However, the pundit referenced Man United’s good record at Anfield since the famous 7-0 drubbing in March 2023, and Liverpool were also widely expected to win on a couple of those occasions.

Pochettino has never lost his first match at any of the five clubs he’s previously managed, and Reds fans might naturally be wary that the players who effectively downed tools under Michael Carrick will suddenly have a spring in their step today.

The good news for Iraola is that he has a mostly fully-fit squad, with Virgil van Dijk and Dominik Szoboszlai overcoming minor issues over the past couple of weeks and Ryan Gravenberch available once more, and there were no fresh injury casualties over the international window.

The Liverpool head coach has had a reasonably good start to his reign but is still waiting on a genuine ‘statement’ victory. That would change if Sutton’s emphatic prediction comes to light, but we’re sure that every Kopite would gladly take a win by any means against our biggest rivals.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Celtic have accepted a reduced ticket allocation for their upcoming visit to Tynecastle despite calls from fans to reject the offer.
  • The Parkhead club, however, have stated that they will contact the Scottish Professional Football League over the matter.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 13:28 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 14:28 EST, 23 November 2026.

Celtic have accepted a reduced ticket allocation for their upcoming visit to Tynecastle despite calls from fans to reject the offer.

The Parkhead club, however, have stated that they will contact the Scottish Professional Football League over the matter.

Celtic will receive 508 tickets for the Premiership encounter on November 29, which will be their first visit to Tynecastle since beating Hearts to the title in the final stages of last season, a victory which resulted in a pitch invasion from some of their fans at Celtic Park.

A Celtic statement read: 'As supporters will know, our allocation for our forthcoming match against Heart of Midlothian at Tynecastle Stadium has been cut by 20 per cent, compared to our previous visit.

'There have been a variety of views expressed to the club from supporters in relation to accepting this allocation. Some groups representing travelling supporters explained to the club that their members did not wish to accept the tickets because of the reduced allocation.

'We have taken that into consideration and also raised their concerns with the home club, who have assured us that they have spoken to Police Scotland.

Hearts had stated that only 508 tickets will be made available for Celtic fans on November 29.

'Having carefully considered all of the circumstances, we can confirm we will accept the allocation of 508 tickets.

'We respect all views and opinions on this matter, and while we are concerned and disappointed at this reduction, and others across recent years, we feel it is important that the team has the backing of our fans within the stadium for an important match.

'We realise the difficulties such a reduction can cause and in light of our discussions with supporters, we can confirm that should any supporter who is successful in the ballot, but does not wish to accept this ticket, then this will NOT affect the away ticket record moving forward.

'We thank our fans for their continued support and can confirm that we will be discussing the matter further with both the home club and the SPFL.'.

Celtic and Rangers formerly received the full Roseburn Stand for their supporters at Tynecastle, which resulted in an allocation of almost 3,500 tickets.

However, that figure was reduced to about 1,250 tickets in the 2021-22 season amid increased demand from home fans after the lockdown, and was further cut by about half.

Only Hibernian now get the full Roseburn Stand in a reciprocal agreement between the Edinburgh rivals.

Tynecastle has a capacity of about 20,000 but Hearts’ attendances are normally around 18,700 as a number of seats are not in use to create a barrier between the home and away fans.

Visiting clubs get about 800 tickets for games at Celtic Park, which has a 60,000 capacity.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has now been revealed what each of the 20 Premier League clubs received from the 2025-26 TV cash payouts.

The information made public via the publication of the EPL’s official 2025-26 annual report.

This report including a breakdown of how much money each of last season’s 20 Premier League clubs banked.

In total, the 20 Premier League clubs received £3,142m for the 2025-26 season.

This is a 10.9% increase on the 2024-25 season.

Banking the most were Arsenal with £198.1m, whilst Wolves received the least with £117.2m.

The Premier League is actually one of the very fairest major European leagues in terms of the gap between which clubs get the very most and very least. Arsenal getting 1.69 x what Wolves received.

This is the breakdown of the total distributions of £3,142m between the 20 Premier League clubs (in order of placings in the Premier League table for the 2025-26 season):.

£198.1m Arsenal £192.7m Man City £191.3m Man U £182.1m Aston Villa £181.6m Liverpool £170.2m Bournemouth £167.7m Sunderland £161.7m Brighton £160.8m Brentford £163.4m Chelsea £154.5m Fulham £153.7m Newcastle United £147.1m Everton £144.2m Leeds £136.4m Palace £135.9 Forest £136.6m Spurs £127.9m West Ham £118.6m Burnley £117.2m Wolves.

According to recent reports, as you can see, some clubs got more than one or more of those that finished above them in the table. This is due to how many times the relative clubs were chosen for live UK coverage, this is the ‘Facility Fees’ portion of the cash.

The Newcastle United total of £153.7m is broken down as:.

UNITED KINGDOM (VIA THE TV DEALS ETC.) Equal Share £31.9m Facility Fees £20.3m Merit £15.4m.

CENTRAL COMMERCIAL Equal Share £11.2m.

OVERSEAS (VIA THE TV DEALS ETC.) Equal Share £56.5m Merit £18.4m.

Newcastle United received £6.5m less than 2024-25 as they fell eight places in the Premier League table. However, it would have been a far bigger drop without the overall 10.9% increase in the entire share out and the fact that NUFC were selected 31 times for UK TV coverage across 2025-26.

The Borussia Dortmund centre-back (19) signed for the Bundesliga giants this summer and has featured 17 times for them since (across all competitions).

Reporting for CaughtOffside’s The Daily Briefing, Mark Brus said: “I’m reliably told by sources with ties to the agents industry that Arsenal and other Premier League clubs have been closely monitoring Gadou for some time. The Frenchman only joined Dortmund this summer after impressing at Red Bull Salzburg, and he also had a spell in PSG’s academy earlier in his career.”.

In a recent development, he went on to add that a source mentioned: “Arsenal got a close look at him yesterday, but the reality is that they have been monitoring Gadou for months. A lot of the top clubs know about him, even if they weren’t ready to move for him yet. I see him developing at Dortmund for a bit longer, but it’s clear how talented he is and if he carries on like this they won’t hold on to him for long.”.

Liverpool, Manchester United and Real Madrid are ‘keen’ on Gadou, but may have to come up against competition from PSG if the player continues his current developmental trajectory.

And that should come as no surprise to onlookers when the Frenchman is putting in top-quality displays of the calibre he produced against Arsenal in the Champions League on Tuesday night.

AC Milan put on a show for their fans at San Siro on Sunday evening as they beat Frosinone 5-1 to move back into the top four.

It was a game that promised entertainment from the early stages, and Milan took command thanks to an own-goal from Gabriele Calvani and a much-needed goal from Goncalo Ramos, before Patrizio Masini scored to halve the deficit.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Recent findings suggest that the Rossoneri ran away with things in the second half, with Ardon Jashari and Alphadjo Cisse netting off the bench before Christian Pulisic got a goal of his own to add some gloss to the scoreline. There were chances to make it an even bigger margin, but five would have to do.

Given that Lazio, Roma, Como and Juventus had all won prior to kick-off, it was key that Milan matched their results to keep up the pressure at the top end of the table, and they did so in emphatic fashion.

According to recent reports, ruben Amorim made just one change to the starting line-up from the side that won against Genoa before the break, with Alphadjo Cisse dropping out and Davide Bartesaghi coming in. It was uncertain from the line-up named what the system would be, as has often been the case with the Portuguese coach so far.

Frosinone started the game better and called Mike Maignan into action inside the first minute with a close-range header that was saved, though the flag was up. Then, a deflected strike from Masini on the edge of the box ended up scraping the upright and going behind for a corner.

However, it was Milan who struck first at San Siro. Luka Modric deserves the plaudits for an outstanding through ball to find Adrien Rabiot’s run in behind, and the Frenchman’s square pass was heading towards Christian Pulisic’s run but was turned into his own net by Calvani, leaving Palmisani rooted.

The frantic pace of the early stages continued, as a lovely exchange between Diego Moreira and Pulisic saw a threatening cross turned behind. A few minutes later, Yunus Musah found Moreira who had a shot deflected for a corner, which Goncalo Ramos rose and met well but headed over the bar.

According to recent reports, frosinone kept providing reminders that they too pose a threat going forward, such as on the quarter-hour mark when Kvernadze surged down the left and got off a low shot from a narrow angle that Maignan had to parry behind. The corner wasn’t properly dealt with, and Cittadini flashed one across the six-yard box that Rabiot had to put into the stands.

According to recent reports, just like with the first goal, Milan punished Frosinone for not making the most of their spell of pressure. Goncalo Ramos was the man who started and finished a flowing counter-attack, robbing Calvani of possession before running towards goal. Musah’s through ball was run onto by the electric Moreira, who found Rabiot, and the Frenchman’s cut-back was tucked away by the Portuguese.

Industry observers note that the two-goal lead was very promptly halved though, as Frosinone got the goal their pressure had threatened. Kvernadze’s run down the left and cut-back from the byline was scuffed onwards by Ghedjemis into the path of Masini, who toe-poked it in at the far post.

In the 34th minute, there was a moment that enraged the Milan players, staff and fans. The referee blew his whistle for a shirt pull on Rabiot just as Milan went through on goal with two men in behind and just the goalkeeper to beat. The official apologised, but it felt like a certain goal had been taken away.

It has been revealed that it was a half played at a hundred miles an hour, and it ended that way too. Pulisic flashed an effort over the bar from a good position, while Davide Bartesaghi’s low cross towards Ramos was cut out in the nick of time as Milan continued to get joy down the flanks.

Amorim opted to make an intriguing change at half-time, bringing off Bartesaghi and replacing him with Ardon Jashari. This change in turn saw Musah shift to left-back, a role that he played against Genoa in the last match, and from minute one.

The change proved to be an absolute masterstroke, as Jashari scored inside three minutes. A ball was sent long to Ramos who knocked it down to Rabiot, whose first touch was a lovely through ball to the Swiss midfield. It looked like he had overrun it with the square option not used, but he lashed a shot in at the near post.

It has been revealed that not long after the goal, Ramos gestured towards the bench that he felt some discomfort. He wanted to play through it but Amorim took no risks, opting to bring Alphadjo Cisse on to lead the line.

There was a rather rare occurrence in the 54th minute, as Milan were awarded an indirect free-kick after Palmisani picked up a back pass from Calvani. Modric laid it off to Rabiot, but the goalkeeper made up for his error with a good save.

Industry observers note that continuing the trend of impact substitutions, Cisse got his ninth goal of the season right on the hour mark. A Frosinone corner was cleared and Pulisic found Moreira who had the Italian for organization, and he finished the through ball by the Belgian past Palmisani with his trademark composure. The offside flag went up, but after a long check the goal was given.

According to recent reports, milan continued to look like scoring every time they got out of their own half, and Pulisic joined the fun in the 68th minute with a goal of his own. Frosinone again left one man back for a corner that was cleared, allowing the American to easily outpace Terzic with a run from inside his own half, dinking over Palmisani to make it 5-1.

In a recent development, with 20 minutes left on the clock, Amorim brought Strahinja Pavlovic and Pervis Estupinan on for Diawara and Musah. The final change saw Omari Hutchinson replace Pulisic.

Pavlovic looked far from 100% when he came on, appearing dizzy at certain moments. The head coach seemed to suggest coming off so as not to risk things, but he played on.

Sources indicate that milan had chances to make the scoreline even more impressive, with Moreira and Hutchinson squandering a couple of chances on the break. However, at full-time the team were rightly applauded by the San Siro crowd.

Breaking: McInnes believes Cup final incentive will fuel Rangers in vital run of fixtures

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.
  • Published: 10:52 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 15:13 EST, 23 November 2026.
  • Rangers boss Derek McInnes insists the incentive of next month's Premier Sports Cup Final can fuel his players as they prepare to embark on a vital run of fixtures.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 10:52 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 15:13 EST, 23 November 2026.

Rangers boss Derek McInnes insists the incentive of next month's Premier Sports Cup Final can fuel his players as they prepare to embark on a vital run of fixtures.

A 2-1 triumph over Motherwell on Saturday night stretched Rangers' unbeaten run to 13 matches after Ryan Naderi struck a late winner at Fir Park.

McInnes' side will host a revitalised Aberdeen at Ibrox on Tuesday night, before two further home matches against Falkirk and Dundee United over the next week.

They will then face a double-header against Hibs, with a league clash at Easter Road swiftly followed by the cup final.

McInnes insists no player is guaranteed their place in the team - and challenged them to earn their place for the Hampden showpiece as they look to win the first trophy of the season.

Sources indicate that 'I think the squad looks strong at the minute,' remarked the Ibrox boss. 'We've got good options and good options from the bench to turn to.

Derek McInnes has led Rangers on a 13-game unbeaten run in all competitions.

'In this little run of fixtures, hopefully everybody will start to play a wee bit more of their part and hopefully more winning performances.

'I don't think I'll mention it [the cup final] too often, but they are not daft, they see that and everybody wants to play in the team.

'Anybody who's in the team needs to keep playing well to stay in the team and anybody who's not in the team needs to train right and take advantage of their minutes.

Sources indicate that 'We make that point often enough. Sometimes you've got to go away to tough venues like Motherwell and do the hard work and get the reward.

'But there's bigger games, more games like cup finals to take part in, so everybody wants to play in that one.

'I'm sure it does us no harm. I think it keeps the fans bubbling along, a chance of silverware, so when it comes along hopefully, as I say, we're in good form.'.

Rangers are on a strong run of form and haven't lost a game since they were dumped out of Europe against Jablonec at the end of August.

The victory over Motherwell maintained their position in second in the table, four points adrift of Celtic with a game in hand.

Up against an Aberdeen side buoyed by their first win under fresh boss Mario Frick at the weekend, McInnes wants his players to keep the pedal to the metal.

'I think it's unusual with five games now away from Ibrox, four in the league and the cup game, and now the fixtures kind of run the other way,' noted the Rangers boss.

'We've got some good fixtures at home but I think we always look at little blocks in the weeks, and where we're looking to try and get to by a certain period, and get certain points and certain targets.

In a recent development, 'But first thing's first now with Aberdeen. We've got to make sure we're a strong home team again. Hopefully we can score a few more goals but, ultimately, as long as we win the game, I'll be happy.

'I think there's always a wee concern when you've got so many away on an international break, but obviously now with the January break gone, this is us working right through to March.

'When you look at those little blocks of games, and where the teams are, it's important that we just put our shoulder to the wheel.

'Every game is going to bring up different challenges and just because we're at Ibrox, it's an advantage, but it doesn't guarantee anything. We've got to use that advantage properly.

In a recent development, 'As I say, we've got some fixtures now ahead of the cup final. Hopefully we can get into the cup final in good form and with some strong performances.'.

Venezuelan striker Kevin Kelsy could be in line to start against Aberdeen.

Kevin Kelsy could be in line for a bigger role this week after fatigue caused by his return from international duty limited his involvement in Saturday's win over Motherwell.

The Venezuela striker was only fit enough for a substitute appearance after enduring a gruelling journey back from a friendly in Russia, with Derek McInnes admitting the travel disruption had taken its toll.

'When you go away on international duty, they go to some far-flung places and playing a friendly in Russia is not the best preparation,' noted the Rangers boss.

In a recent development, 'There was a point on Thursday morning when we were really worried about whether he was getting back. To have ten-and-a-half hours in an airport all day Thursday isn't ideal preparation.

Recent findings suggest that 'He was gubbed on Friday. He was very tired when he spoke to me and told me he hadn't really slept.

'It's been a bit unusual, the preparation. We sent him home early on Friday to get a good sleep and look after himself, but we just made the call we thought was the right thing to do.

'We needed everybody at it on Saturday and we've got a massive week ahead of us where he can play his part, hopefully from the start in one or two of these games.'.

#118286. Tech Report: “Why didn’t they check?” – Pochettino still fuming over refereeing decision in Liverpool romp

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (473 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Empireofthekop ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: “Why didn’t they check?” – Pochettino still fuming over refereeing decision in Liverpool romp

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (473 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Empireofthekop

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mauricio Pochettino continues to rage over decisions which he feels went against his team in the 4-0 drubbing by Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday.
  • Manchester United were reduced to 10 men inside seven minutes when Leny Yoro barged into Alexander Isak and was adjudged to have denied a clear goalscoring opportunity.
  • Dominik Szoboszlai opened the scoring from the resulting free kick, although the Red Devils head coach complained that Bradley Barcola was interfering with the visitors’ defensive wall from the set piece.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mauricio Pochettino continues to rage over decisions which he feels went against his team in the 4-0 drubbing by Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday.

Manchester United were reduced to 10 men inside seven minutes when Leny Yoro barged into Alexander Isak and was adjudged to have denied a clear goalscoring opportunity. The red card has since been overturned on the basis that the Reds striker was unlikely to get to the ball had he not been impeded.

Dominik Szoboszlai opened the scoring from the resulting free kick, although the Red Devils head coach complained that Bradley Barcola was interfering with the visitors’ defensive wall from the set piece.

Speaking to the media ahead of Man United’s Champions League clash against Sporting Lisbon, Pochettino raged (via Liverpool Echo): “No-one talked about that the goal wasn’t legal. They should disallow the goal because Barcola was touching our wall.

In a recent development, “[Eberechi] Eze, last season for Palace [against Chelsea], when Eze scored, [it was disallowed]. Why didn’t they check the VAR, check the goal? That must be disallowed.

“[I] need to defend my players and my club. Where are the three points? We need to think a little more deep in the way that we use the technology.”.

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

While Pochettino might feel vindicated over his grievances about Yoro’s red card now that the decision has been overturned on appeal, he’s clutching at straws by complaining about the free kick from which Szoboszlai scored.

Replays show that it was actually Fernandes who pushed Barcola out of the way when the ball was struck, and the Liverpool forward most certainly isn’t at fault for how poorly the Man United defensive wall was set up.

Bruno literally pushed Barcola into the wall 😂😂😂😂 these lot are losing the plot.pic.twitter.com/tjPFU56OTg https://t.co/bJWXQfmfUk.

— LB (@LBLFC_) November 24, 2026.

Even though his team were very much discommoded by the early red card, their response to that setback was still a meek surrender, and that’s what should concern their head coach the most rather than blaming opposition players.

The Red Devils still had more than 80 minutes to reorganise and try to get a result, and while they did stem the tide for a large chunk of the game at 2-0, they were still indebted to wasteful finishing from the home side that the final score wasn’t even more emphatic.

While Pochettino moans, Liverpool will be busy preparing for their own Champions League clash away to Club Brugge, followed by the small matter of the Merseyside derby on Sunday.

#118285. Mikel Arteta issues clear warning to Arsenal loanee Ethan Nwaneri ahead of Champions League clash

📖 Baca
General ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

Mikel Arteta issues clear warning to Arsenal loanee Ethan Nwaneri ahead of Champions League clash

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (440 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Lewis Blain | 24 Nov 2026 07:16.
  • Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has warned Ethan Nwaneri that brief flashes of quality will not be enough to secure regular football at Borussia Dortmund.
  • The record-breaking 19-year-old joined the Bundesliga leaders on loan from the Gunners in the summer, but has struggled for opportunities in recent weeks.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Blain | 24 Nov 2026 07:16.

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has warned Ethan Nwaneri that brief flashes of quality will not be enough to secure regular football at Borussia Dortmund.

The record-breaking 19-year-old joined the Bundesliga leaders on loan from the Gunners in the summer, but has struggled for opportunities in recent weeks.

Nwaneri could now face his parent club in Tuesday's Champions League meeting in north London, with Arteta making his expectations clear.

Nwaneri initially enjoyed opportunities in Niko Kovac's starting lineup after arriving in Germany, but his involvement has since diminished significantly.

The versatile attacking midfielder has not started a match in over a month and has played just five minutes across Dortmund's last three Bundesliga fixtures.

Arteta believes the teenager must show greater consistency to establish himself at the highest level, insisting that occasional impressive performances are not enough.

"We're talking here about the highest level in Europe," the Arsenal boss stated (via the Evening Standard). "You can just shine in moments, but moments are not enough. Now you need to show the consistency.".

The Spaniard also stressed that Nwaneri must earn his place in a talented Dortmund squad, rather than expect opportunities because of his Arsenal background.

"He needs to earn the right to play," Arteta added, explaining that joining a major European club does not automatically guarantee minutes.

Arteta remains convinced that Nwaneri has the mentality and quality to succeed, but acknowledged that his loan spells at Marseille and Dortmund form part of a challenging development journey.

Arsenal are understood to have the option to recall the youngster in January if his situation does not improve, with Arteta currently unconvinced that the Dortmund move is delivering the desired benefits.

Nwaneri is eligible to feature against his parent club on Tuesday, although Dortmund's strong form makes a starting place appear unlikely.

Nevertheless, the opportunity to face Arsenal off the bench could provide the teenager with an ideal platform to respond to Arteta's comments, particularly after his recent lack of involvement.

The Gunners boss has challenged him to show consistency and earn his place, rather than rely on occasional moments of quality. A positive contribution against the Premier League champions would certainly help his case.

Should Nwaneri find the net, he could join a select group of players to score against their parent clubs while on loan, including James Rodriguez against Real Madrid and Philippe Coutinho against Barcelona during their respective spells at Bayern Munich.

It would be a significant way to make his mark, although simply earning meaningful minutes against Arsenal would represent an encouraging step in his Dortmund journey.

The Original Article was published on 23 September 2026.

Correction to: Nature https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-11007-3 Published online 23 September 2026.

In the version of the article initially published, in the Abstract, “Biogeography” section and Conclusion, the epoch in which bats originated was given as the “late Palaeocene” but should have been “late Cretaceous/early Palaeocene”. This has now been corrected in the HTML and PDF versions of this article.

#118282. Latest Update: Scotland's World Cup prize must not become a missed opportunity

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (573 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dailymail ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: Scotland's World Cup prize must not become a missed opportunity

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (573 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 15:23 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 15:36 EST, 23 November 2026.
  • Confirmation that Scotland will co-host the 2035 FIFA Women’s World Cup is an undoubted boost for the game in this country.
  • Staging a global showpiece with England, Wales and Northern Ireland is indeed a potential game-changer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 15:23 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 15:36 EST, 23 November 2026.

Confirmation that Scotland will co-host the 2035 FIFA Women’s World Cup is an undoubted boost for the game in this country.

Staging a global showpiece with England, Wales and Northern Ireland is indeed a potential game-changer.

The joint bid projected that the competition would attract 3.5billion viewers worldwide. And that 4.5m tickets would be sold across the host nations.

But the key for Scotland will be the impact it has on girls taking up the sport, supporters watching it and professionals playing it north of the Border.

Scotland captain Caroline Weir has already described it as a ‘pivotal’ moment, a ‘real opportunity’ to drive momentum and reach another level, domestically and internationally.

She’s right. It is an opportunity, of the once-in-a-lifetime variety, but a word of caution is in order. Opportunities are not enough in themselves to be transformative.

They have to be embraced, exploited and squeezed for all they are worth so that every last drop of their potential is properly fulfilled.

Star player Caroline Weir believes co-hosting the World Cup could be pivotal for women's football in Scotland.

It would be criminal if the powers-that-be got complacent about this priceless gift and made assumptions about its long-term legacy.

More players, more fans and more media coverage would be hugely exciting, but it will all be wasted if not supported by facilities, coaches and the safeguarding that goes with it.

It has happened before. Interest in athletics rocketed after Glasgow 2014, but a poor infrastructure, which continued to rely on volunteers, prevented a grassroots boom.

And how many times have we heard Judy Murray complain that Scottish tennis squandered the opportunity presented to it by her son, Andy?

In a recent development, scotland’s women played at the World Cup in 2019. Their game has grown since then, but the national side have not been to another major tournament and the domestic product is still a shadow of its English counterpart.

Only a handful of Scottish teams have full-time players. The wages are way behind those on offer down south. And professional men’s clubs could do much, much more to develop the sport. It’s no wonder the Scottish league can’t keep its better players.

The opposite is true in England, where the success of the national team is often attributed to the level of investment by the FA and the backing of sponsors across the country.

The good news is that Scotland have made a start on that front with something called Project 2035, which aims to transform girls' and women’s football over the next decade.

The Scottish government has stumped up an initial £250,000 to help with the 10-year blueprint, which outlined a number of key objectives earlier this month.

They want to grow participation at grassroots level, increase the number of women working in football - as coaches, leaders and decision-makers - and quadruple the number of fans. The hope also is that Scotland will progress beyond the group stage of at least one World Cup by 2035.

Recent findings suggest that having those ambitions is one thing; making good on them is quite another. The government, the league, clubs and the ruling body: all should be thrilled by this opportunity but they should also feel the pressure that it brings. For it is their responsibility, their duty, to make the most of it.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Chelsea have decided against making an immediate change in the dugout despite growing pressure on manager Xabi Alonso.
  • The Blues have won just one of their last five matches, with a 4-1 defeat to Leeds United at Stamford Bridge only intensifying scrutiny of the Spaniard.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Blain | 24 Nov 2026 07:38.

Chelsea have decided against making an immediate change in the dugout despite growing pressure on manager Xabi Alonso.

The Blues have won just one of their last five matches, with a 4-1 defeat to Leeds United at Stamford Bridge only intensifying scrutiny of the Spaniard.

However, the club hierarchy are understood to remain keen to give their summer appointment time, although the next few fixtures could prove crucial.

Chelsea's board have no immediate plans to sack Alonso, but the 44-year-old is under pressure to deliver results in the coming matches, according to new reports.

The Blues face Nottingham Forest and Crystal Palace next, before a demanding run of fixtures against Liverpool, Manchester City and Aston Villa. The three matches before Christmas could "make or break" Alonso's future at Stamford Bridge.

Chelsea right now sit eighth in the Premier League table, with supporters having already voiced their frustration during the defeat to Leeds.

There are also concerns of a "mutiny" behind the scenes, with it believed that several players are unhappy with Alonso's coaching methods at the training ground and that there is a "terrible atmosphere in the dressing room".

Nevertheless, the hierarchy are understood to believe that injuries have contributed to the team's struggles. Joao Pedro has been absent since the middle of October with a thigh problem, having been an crucial figure earlier in the campaign.

The club are hopeful that his return could help spark an improvement in results, although the pressure on Alonso is unlikely to disappear unless performances improve.

Clearlake have made managerial changes a regular feature of their Chelsea project, but dismissing Alonso just months into his tenure would risk repeating a familiar cycle at Stamford Bridge.

The Spaniard is still relatively early into his reign and has had to contend with key absences, particularly Pedro and captain Reece James. Both are usual starters who could make a significant difference to the side, especially in a system that relies on their respective qualities.

The reported dressing-room discontent is concerning, however, and Alonso will need to address that quickly, but it should not automatically mean his position is untenable.

According to recent reports, managers need time to implement their ideas, build relationships and establish consistency. Chelsea have invested in Alonso and should allow him to demonstrate what he can achieve with a fitter squad.

The upcoming fixtures will undoubtedly test that patience, but another change of manager so early in the process would hardly represent a convincing long-term strategy.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Andoni Iraola has noted that he thoroughly enjoyed his analysis of Club Brugge ahead of Liverpool’s Champions League fixture against the Belgian outfit tonight.

It’s the first time in 48 years that the teams have faced each other, with all three of their previous meetings coming in European finals – the two-legged 1976 UEFA Cup showpiece and the European Cup decider two years later (both of which the Reds won).

The sides have near-identical records going into the game at the Jan Breydel Stadium, with both on nine points and a +4 goal difference, and victory for either could catapult them into the top four of the league phase standings.

Speaking in his pre-match press conference on Tuesday, Iraola was notaly effusive in his praise of Club Brugge and is expecting a highly entertaining spectacle in Belgium.

Recent findings suggest that the Liverpool head coach said (via liverpoolfc.com): “It’s not that they surprised me. I knew they were very good, but honestly I’ve enjoyed analysing them. Sometimes you have to analyse a team, you have to watch a lot of games and it’s a little bit boring!

“With Brugge that definitely hasn’t happened. They are a very attractive team. They are very energetic, everyone runs, very aggressive in the press. They are coming with an incredible run of games. I think it’s 10 wins and a draw in the last 11. Also big, big games in those – Inter Milan, PSV away.

(Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images).

Industry observers note that “I think we will have to be at a very, very good level otherwise it’s going to be very difficult. They have players that can make the difference.

In a recent development, “I expect quite an open game because they are aggressive and we are aggressive. We want to press; they want to press. Probably there will be spaces in the game and I hope we can win those one-v-ones, individual battles that definitely tomorrow we are going to see, yes.”.

Industry observers note that want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

This might seem like classic pre-match diplomacy on Iraola’s part, but Club Brugge’s numbers from this season indicate that the Basque’s praise is very much justified.

Ivan Leko’s side have scored 45 goals in their 18 matches so far this term (2.5 per game), including 11 in their four Champions League outings (2.75 per game), including a memorable 4-3 triumph away to Inter Milan (who Liverpool will face at San Siro in January).

They’re scored three or more goals in seven of their 12 league matches in 2026/27, an impressive return even allowing for the quality of opposition in the Belgian top flight, and they’ve one forward who’s responsible for just over a third of their goals in the current campaign.

(Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images).

Nicolo Tresoldi has 16 goals from 18 games, including a hat-trick in the aforementioned win against Inter, and his last five league outings have seen him score seven times (Transfermarkt).

Club Brugge will be aware that Liverpool’s concession record in the Champions League this term has been pitiful, with 10 goals shipped across their four matches and three each in the games against LASK, Villarreal and Fenerbahce.

Iraola may have enjoyed analysing tonight’s opponents over the past few days, but he won’t be too enamoured if they put the Reds to the sword in Belgium. The Merseysiders can’t say they haven’t been forewarned.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Newcastle United suffered a painful, chastening defeat, comprehensively beaten by Coventry City in a performance that should send a shudder of fear through Tyneside.

It was a dreadful night for the visitors, who conceded four goals for the second successive away game. The manner in which they fell apart was damning. Whatever the supposed style of play, it is not good to watch: long balls are pumped forward for short strikers to chase or compete for in the air against far taller centre-backs. Away from home, it is becoming ineffective.

Newcastle are too easy to create chances against and there is not much that gets you excited when they attack.

It has been revealed that matthias Jaissle’s side did create chances against Coventry, but are not clinical and do not inspire confidence they can be with the players they have. Defensively, they escaped earlier in the season, but are now being exposed and punished. “Not good enough in both boxes,” was Jaissle’s blunt verdict. “To concede eight goals in two away games is not good enough.”.

According to recent reports, matthias Jaissle on this evening's defeat at the Coventry Building Society Arena. https://t.co/216NW6Laz8.

Newcastle’s misery was in stark contrast to the joyous celebrations from Coventry. This was a thoroughly deserved first home win of the season for Frank Lampard’s side.

According to recent reports, “It was an outstanding performance,” the manager said. “We knew we would have to suffer at times against a team like Newcastle. But we were really good at the basics, winning the second balls, winning the duels, those moments are critical. It’s not always about pretty patterns, it’s about work ethic.”.

The win lifts Coventry level on points with Manchester United and will give them fresh confidence at this level. This could be the start of something special for them.

As for Newcastle, this raises uncomfortable questions about their summer recruitment, with so many expensive players on the bench or playing badly. It also means people will query whether Jaissle’s implementation of “vertical football” is working. The fact Lampard talked so openly about winning the duels to set up the win will anger the German.

Jaissle can point to two bad misses from one of the new arrivals, Matias Fernandez-Pardo, a £51m buy from Lille, in the first half. But his team are too easy to play through and the defence is an accident waiting to happen.

In a recent development, even after Sven Botman’s stunning strike offered them a way back into the game, they capitulated at the back as Lewis Hall – who was off colour all evening – and Joelinton’s mistakes gift-wrapped a third for Ellis Simms. A fourth followed for Stephen Mfuni.

According to recent reports, ellis Simms off the bench with a massive impact! 💥 https://t.co/XynFVxwERV.

You can get a sense of what sort of mode a team are in within the first few passages of play and Newcastle were not sharp or precise. It was sloppy.

That was certainly true of goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek, who was off his line in no-man’s land trying to snuff out a through ball that he was not going to get. He stood up to deflect it away, but then rashly chased after it, diving at full stretch at the feet of Coventry’s Sidiki Cherif and failing to get the ball. Jack Rudoni coolly sent the Czech goalkeeper the wrong way from the spot.

Newcastle had been awful in their last away game at Leeds, another 4-1 thrashing, and there were many of the same faults on display.

In a recent development, it was not a good first half for Fernandez-Pardo up top. They are mystified in Belgium why he believes he is a centre-forward rather than a winger and he did not do himself any favours here. Newcastle’s best move of the game resulted in Lewis Miley playing in Jacob Murphy down the left. His cutback was perfect for Fernandez-Pardo to sweep home at the near post but instead of trying to make contact, he dummied it, thinking Harvey Barnes was better placed. He was not. It was a baffling piece of centre-forward play.

It had been the easiest 40 minutes Lampard’s side have had since they were promoted, but Newcastle still should have scored before the break.

According to recent reports, nico González spotted the run of Fernandez-Pardo through the middle. He wriggled clear of Bobby Thomas and sat down goalkeeper Carl Rushworth, but the Coventry centre-back got back to block his shot.

Newcastle pressed the self-destruct button early in the second half. A long throw into the box was half cleared. There was a half-hearted attempt to close Cherif down from Yoane Wissa and then a shot that somehow went through a crowd of three Newcastle defenders, including the legs of Botman, and nestled in the bottom corner.

Sidiki Cherif with a STUNNING finish on his first Premier League start! 🤩 https://t.co/EoTB8VCHuR.

Recent findings suggest that it should have been three. Again Wissa was partly to blame, losing the ball in midfield to set Coventry on the counter-attack. When Botman made a mess of a clearance it spun perfectly into the path of Cherif. The net should have bulged but the £20m summer signing from Fenerbahce scuffed wide.

The visitors needed something special to get back into it and it came from the most unlikely of sources as Botman unleashed a rocket from 25 yards.

Sven Botman, that is SENSATIONAL! 🤯 https://t.co/GalkqMs5ZE.

In a flash the balance of play shifted in Newcastle’s favour. They poured forward in search of the equaliser. Jaissle switched to a 4-4-2 with Will Osula joining Fernandez-Pardo up front, but instead of pulling level, Coventry pulled further ahead.

"We need to improve the things we can control, and right now that's a lot" 🗣️ Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle expresses his disappointment after his side's loss to Coventry 👇 https://t.co/fatJkZYyRM.

According to recent reports, very, very satisfying. It’s so hard to win. We played like the team we want to be here. A team you look at and go there’s so much energy and spirit in the group. We know we are going to have to suffer this season, when we don’t have a lot of the ball. We have to understand it. The level is what it is.

The work ethic, the belief. You get what you deserve. Great finishes. We haven’t quite had the rub of the green this season and that might have helped us nick a couple of more points. I’m a firm believer that you keep going. It was a complete performance. We’ve got to keep our feet on the ground because we’re going to have to do 30+ of those but it’s a great feeling for the players.

Recent findings suggest that [Cherif] is very, very exciting because he is so young. He has got a really good manner. He wants to train, he wants to learn. He’s quite quiet but on the pitch he demonstrates a lot of personality. When you see the quality of the strike and the hold-up play, there’s a lot to come from him.

A win for Newcastle United this evening will take Matthias Jaissle’s side up to fourth in the Premier League and vindicate the members of the club’s hierarchy who insisted they had appointed an elite manager to replace Eddie Howe.

It will also suggest they got their summer rebuild right and everything will point to an exciting future for a fresh look team.

Yet, should Newcastle lose against a Coventry City side – newly promoted to the top flight and yet to win at home this season – ripples of discontent will spread through the fanbase and everything about the summer, from managerial appointment to player recruitment will be called into question.

According to recent reports, that may seem like an odd thing to write given how wildly different those reactions are but that is where Newcastle find themselves at the moment. We do not actually know if they are any good or what the expectations should be for a young team with a rookie Premier League head coach.

There remains an undercurrent of anxiety among supporters who have seen so many of their best players leave over the last 12 months and be replaced by young, emerging talent from across Europe.

When Brian Kilcline was at Notts County, the manager Jimmy Sirrel became a little perturbed by the nickname his young centre-back had carried since his school days. It might have been nice alliteration, but “Killer Kilcline” was not exactly the image he wanted his team to portray.

“Also the lads shouting, ‘get him Killer’ tended to alert referees,” Kilcline recalls.

So Sirrel decided he would put it to the County fans. He organised a competition to establish a better moniker for his foursquare defender.

Industry observers note that “You know what they came up with?” Kilcline claims. “Curly Wurly. Like the chocolate bar. It was to do with my hair, which was naturally curled. By the way, it was never a perm. But I mean, come on. I can’t imagine Curly Wurly would have intimidated anyone.”.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League match between Coventry City and Newcastle United from the Ricoh Arena. Newcastle have played only once there in the league – a 4-1 victory in the Championship back in 2010 when Chris Hughton’s side stormed the league. Their last top-flight visit to the city was way back in 2000, the year Cov’s 34-season spell in the top division ended. Alan Shearer Kevin Gallacher scored at Highfield Road on that occasion, a year after they were sent packing 4-1 by Gordon Strachan’s side by virtue of goals from Carlton Palmer, Paul Williams, Robbie Keane and Mustapha Hadji.

Today’s visit begins with Newcastle in 11th, having bounced back from their Monday night mauling at Elland Road to beat Hull 23 days ago. So bunched is the table, though, that victory tonight would propel them up to fourth. Coventry, by contrast, are 19th after one win and four defeats from their opening five games. If they win they would join Manchester United on six points and leap to 14th, one place ahead of Nottingham Forest, the team they beat last time out before the international break.

Frank Lampard’s side responded superbly after being hammered 5-0 by Brighton in their last home game, tightening up in midfield and defence and finding precisely Forest’s weak spots that Oliver Glasner has been unable so far to armour-plate. Taiwo Awoniyi, who was sent off during that defeat by Brighton, is absent serving the second leg of his three-match suspension and Hajii Wright and Aurele Amenda are still some way off returning. Tino Livramento pulled out of the England camp with injury and is likely to be sidelined for a while longer but Matthias Jaissle was more optimistic about his raft of other doubts: William Osula, Lewis Miley, Amar Dedic, club captain Dan Burn, Anthony Elanga and Jacob Ramsey.

Arsenal: 'Much more complete' - how Madueke has grown and become a key man amid injuries

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Axel Clody | 24 Nov 2026 07:45.
  • Noni Madueke's signing by Arsenal divided opinion before the forward had even stepped onto the pitch.
  • Arriving from Chelsea for £50m, the Englishman joined a squad that already had Bukayo Saka as the owner of the right wing and had to justify an investment in a player who initially seemed destined to be a back-up.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Axel Clody | 24 Nov 2026 07:45.

Noni Madueke's signing by Arsenal divided opinion before the forward had even stepped onto the pitch.

Arriving from Chelsea for £50m, the Englishman joined a squad that already had Bukayo Saka as the owner of the right wing and had to justify an investment in a player who initially seemed destined to be a back-up.

It has been revealed that A little over a year later, the debate is taking on another dimension. With Saka injured, Madueke has been given a longer run of opportunities and has taken the chance. As well as goals and assists, he has contributed in different roles on both sides of the pitch. The 2-2 draw with Newcastle, in which he scored the goal that earned Arsenal a point, was another example of this development.

Sources indicate that mikel Arteta has noticed a change that goes beyond productivity. In a press conference, the manager highlighted the variety that the forward has added to the team's play and his contribution without the ball. And Madueke's growth has followed a concrete path.

Industry observers note that madueke has very specific characteristics. Left-footed and explosive, he likes to receive the ball wide on the right, run at the full-back and carry the ball towards the box to shoot or find a team-mate. His short burst of acceleration and ability to change direction make his movements hard to defend when he receives the ball in equal-numbers situations.

Industry observers note that that characteristic was already visible at Chelsea. In the 2024-25 season, he was one of the Premier League players who carried the ball into the box the most and created danger mainly through individual runs. The problem was inconsistency in execution: he did not always choose the best moment. Arteta acknowledged the change.

'He is becoming decisive in games, and that is what we need from our forward players. And he is doing it in several ways, which is something I really like. He has added variety and a lot more connection to his game' - Arteta noted.

The numbers help to gauge the growth. According to FotMob's analysis for the 2026-27 Premier League, Madueke creates 3.6 chances per 90 minutes, compared with 1.5 for Saka. It is a significant difference, although it is vital to consider that Saka has played fewer minutes.

Recent findings suggest that the improvement also indicates in his ability to contribute without the ball. According to Arteta, Madueke does not always need to receive the ball at his feet to take part in the move.

Industry observers note that 'And yes, I also love his intensity without the ball. So, I would say he is becoming a much more complete player, and I think he is enjoying it a lot' - Arteta mentioned.

According to recent reports, the evolution, therefore, is not about abandoning the dribble but about knowing when to use it. Madueke remains a player of individual initiative, only now he seems to understand better how his actions can connect with the collective workings of the team.

Sources indicate that the comparison with Saka is inevitable, but the two are not identical players. Both are left-footed and prefer to start from the right to cut inside, but they do so in different ways.

According to recent reports, saka is more refined in decision-making. He has excellent ball control, protects possession under pressure and alternates between carries, short passes and crosses very naturally. His ability to draw two markers and find the free team-mate is also one of Arsenal's main attacking tools.

Industry observers note that madueke, for his part, offers more explosiveness in the first movement and tends to look for the individual duel more often. He is a more vertical player, who likes to accelerate and attack the space left by the full-back. When he is confident, he can disorganise a defence without depending on a long build-up.

Sources indicate that the creation data helps illustrate this difference. As well as outperforming Saka in chances created per 90 minutes in FotMob's analysis, Madueke also shows a greater volume of dribbles and progressive carries per minute in another statistical comparison this season. Saka, on the other hand, keeps the advantage in shooting and defensive contribution indicators. They are complementary profiles, not necessarily competitors for a single way of playing.

This difference is valuable for Arteta. Against opponents who defend in a low block, Saka can be more useful to control possession, combine with the midfielders and find the pass that dismantles the marking. Madueke can offer a more direct threat, attacking the full-back and creating situations of individual imbalance.

The Englishman has also shown that he can play on the left, a role he performed when Christos Tzolis was unavailable. There, he needs to adapt his movements: instead of cutting inside with his dominant foot, he can look for the byline and cross with his right. It is not necessarily his ideal position, but the versatility widens Arteta's options and prevents the team from depending on a single alternative for each side.

In a recent development, the competition with Saka, therefore, does not need to be understood as an attempt to take the starter's place. Arsenal need more than one player capable of deciding matches, especially in a long season, with the Premier League, the Champions League and domestic cups. The point is that Madueke is starting to offer arguments to be considered more than a simple replacement.

According to recent reports, one detail of this transformation happened away from Arsenal. After being left out of an England squad, Madueke decided to use the international break to train individually. Instead of treating the period as a chance to rest, the forward sought out a specific preparation programme.

Recent findings suggest that arteta highlighted the player's reaction as an example for the rest of the squad. The manager said that Madueke came back from the break as a different athlete, determined not to accept the situation he was in.

Madueke at Arsenal, season by season.

Premier League 2025-26 vs. 2026-27, per-90 averages.

In a recent development, premier League games only. Because the seasons have different numbers of minutes, the comparison uses per-90 averages; the total appears below each average. The change compares the averages. Madueke has not yet provided an assist in the Premier League in 2026-27. Data up to 21 November 2026 (matchweek 11).

'He went away, decided to train, came back, and he was a different Noni. You could sense that he meant business, and he was not going to accept that situation. Since then, he has been incredible' - Arteta explained, commenting on the player's change of attitude.

In a recent development, the individual work, however, did not start now. In an interview with Sky Sports, Madueke revealed that he has been working for years with specialist coach Saul Isaksson-Hurst, since his time at PSV. The partnership involves technical improvement and individual development, with special attention to the ability to be more decisive in the final third.

It has been revealed that the result has shown up in the numbers: his average of chances created has more than doubled compared with last season, reaching 3.57 per 90 minutes in the Premier League. His dribble success rate has risen from 50% to 55%, while his passing accuracy has gone from 78% to 87%. In open-play crosses, his success rate has jumped from 14% to 33%.

According to recent reports, these numbers help explain why Arteta talks about a more complete player. Madueke has not stopped looking for the dribble, but he has started to execute better other actions that previously could limit his influence. The progress has come from different reasons and paths, but the result has arrived and is evident in the current season.

Gerry Cardinale gave his thoughts after watching his AC Milan side run riot against Frosinone at San Siro this evening.

In a recent development, it has been yet another few days where the Milan owner has made his presence felt. After landing in Italy, he was at Milanello and Casa Milan on Saturday for a series of vital meetings with the management and the squad, and then he watched first hand as the Rossoneri won tonight.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

An own-goal from Gabriele Calvani got the scoring going, before Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic all scored in the 5-1 rout of Frosinone. It could have been more in truth, but it was another display of the level this team can play at.

Cardinale was interviewed by Michael Cuomo of TeleLombardia after the final whistle having made his way down from the stands, and his comments were relayed by MilanNews.

How happy is he? Is he satisfied?

Recent findings suggest that “Well, I’m never satisfied, but the results speak for themselves. The boys were fantastic tonight. I hope you’re happy. I hope the fans are happy. I think the team is coming together really well.

Sources indicate that “It’s a game, let’s keep it under control, but I’m really proud of the boys. This is a team. It’s a team that wants to win until the end.”.

Can you dream of winning the Scudetto?

“Look, it’s November. We still have a long way to go. But we want to see improvements in every match. This weekend was very interesting if you look at the kind of results we’ve had. You can see that something is changing in Serie A.

It has been revealed that “I was very happy to see us not just win, but win by that margin. And so, we have to build on that, but as Amorim notes, every match is something to build on, and we have a long way to go. I personally still expect us to compete for the Scudetto, but it’s a long way off. One match at a time.

“Now the focus is on the Europa League. Yes, and as Ruben said, we have to do both. European competitions are vital. Everything is a test. If you want to win a Scudetto, you have to do it all the way, and that’s what we’ll do.”.

Could signings arrive in January?

Industry observers note that “Again: January is just another stage. As you know, the January transfer window is complicated. You have to be disciplined. You can’t just jump into something randomly. The only thing that will happen under my ownership is that every time we play in the transfer market, we’ll play to win.

“That’s the theme. That’s the theme I stated at the beginning of this year. So, if we make a move in any transfer window, January or June, it will be a move that will count.”.

Liverpool lost their 100% record in this season’s Champions League with defeat at Fenerbahce three weeks ago, and they’ll be aiming to bounce back tonight with victory away to Club Brugge.

For Reds fans of a certain vintage, the Belgian outfit will evoke happy memories of the triumphant 1976 UEFA Cup final and 1978 European Cup final, with this being the first meeting since the latter success at Wembley.

Andoni Iraola’s satisfaction at Sunday’s 4-0 drubbing of Manchester United has been tempered by ongoing injuries to Cody Gakpo and Ryan Gravenberch, with no return date set for the midfielder  as he continues to struggle with a heel problem.

The Liverpool head coach spoke of how he ‘enjoyed analysing’ Club Brugge, who go into this game level on points and goal difference with the Reds and have a red-hot striker in Nicolo Tresoldi, who’s already netted 16 times this season (including a hat-trick against Inter Milan).

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

Iraola has made three changes from the starting XI which thumped Man United on Sunday.

Alisson Becker continues between the sticks, and there’s one change to the defence. It’s a surprising one, too, with Virgil van Dijk omitted from the line-up to allow for the reintroduction of Jeremie Frimpong at right-back.

Ronald Araujo duly shuffles across to centre-back to partner Jeremy Jacquet, with Milos Kerkez on the left.

One alteration in midfield sees Trey Nyoni come in for Alexis Mac Allister, with the teenager lining up next to Dominik Szoboszlai.

The third and final change to the starting XI sees Victor Munoz replace Rio Ngumoha in attack, with Florian Wirtz, Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak all keeping their places.

The trio who are cut from the line-up are all on the substitutes’ bench, which also includes a mixture of youth (Jayden Danns, James McConnell, Lewis Koumas, Luke Chambers) and experience (Joe Gomez, Kostas Tsimikas, Freddie Woodman).
